title: Supervisor, In-Flight Service
description:
Our role is to brighten up everyday life with the joy of vacation. At Air Transat, we work with respect, diversity and pride and belong to one of the largest integrated tourism companies in the world. When you choose Air Transat, you benefit from competitive compensation, a full range of benefits and a travel benefits program.

Reporting to the Base Manager, the In-Flight Service Supervisor has an everyday crucial role towards the success of the cabin crew members. The In-Flight Service Supervisor is responsible for motivating, informing and coaching all crew members on a daily basis. They contribute to the promotion of a professional, motivating and pleasant work environment while ensuring the application of the company standards and regulations in place.

The In-Flight Service Supervisor is at the heart of the operations to support the teams, to detect any problems and/or irregularities surrounding the in-flight operations and to propose visionary solutions, while keeping in mind the reality of the cabin crew members. The In-Flight Service Supervisor is fully aware of the reality surrounding daily operations and is actively involved in the continuous improvement of processes and procedures surrounding the customer and employee experience.

The responsibilities of the in-flight service supervisor can be categorized into two major objectives

Operational:

  • Conducts regular and sporadic operational visits to validate compliance with Canadian Aviation Regulations, workplace safety and company service standards. These extensive checks may be at the gates and in-flight as an active crew member.
  • Actively participates in the smooth running of operations to ensure on-time performance, while continuously reading the internal organizational environment to identify potential risks, opportunities and threats.
  • Reviews the various administrative reports that are sent by the cabin crew members (flight reports, accident/passenger incident reports, injury reports, etc.) in order to follow up with the various internal stakeholders;
  • Administers Flight Attendant expense accounts and authorizes various flight attendant claims and premiums.
  • Participates in the emergency response plan and supports operations in irregular and/or emergency situations.

Labor Relations:

  • Accompanies and contributes to the development of cabin crew members so that they reach and exceed the expected performance levels through a constructive approach in line with the company culture;
  • Monitor the attendance records of cabin crew members, while applying the medical control policy.
  • In collaboration with the Labour Relations Advisors, the In-Flight Service Supervisor is called upon to investigate disciplinary/administrative cases, to attend meetings and to decide on the validity of certain disciplinary/administrative cases.
  • Participates in the hiring process for cabin crew members.
  • Represents the employer on one or more of the organization's local committees (Health and Safety, service, uniform, etc.).
  • Minimum of five (5) years experience in the airline industry.
  • Two (2) years of experience in employee management/supervision, in a unionized environment (an important asset).
  • Ability and experience with Microsoft tools (Outlook, Excel, Word, Teams).
  • Excellent oral and written English and French preferred.
  • Flexible schedule and irregular hours are an integral part of the job (mornings, evenings, weekends and holidays) in addition to offering periods of availability to be on call.
  • Willingness to travel internationally using a valid Canadian passport.
  • Successfully complete the initial cabin crew training and maintain qualifications.
  • Must be able to obtain and maintain an airport restricted area identification card (requires a 5-year traceable history, criminal background check and Canadian citizenship or permanent resident card).

Competency

  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Possesses strong leadership and motivation skills.
  • Ability to manage several files at once by having a good organizational capacity.
  • Must be able to manage priorities well.
  • Ability to adapt to change.
  • Good judgment and discretion.
  • Demonstrate rigor, integrity, autonomy and professionalism.

title: Security Engineer
description:
The application window is expected to close on: 09/11/2026

Job posting may be removed earlier if the position is filled or if a sufficient number of applications are received.

Meet the Team

Acacia (part of Cisco) is a market leader in high-speed coherent optical transceivers, pioneering technology that powers the world’s hyperscale data centers. The internal Acacia IT team is focused on the exciting challenge of architecting, building, and maintaining the infrastructure that allows our engineers to connect people and systems across the globe. We are a collaborative, high-energy group that thrives on innovation, and as the demands of our business grow, so does our need for proactive security leadership. We value technical curiosity and a "security-first" approach that balances robust protection with the agility required in a fast-paced technology environment.

Your Impact

As a Security Engineer on the Acacia IT Operations team, you will drive day-to-day security operations (focusing on identity security, vulnerability management, and endpoint protection) to ensure a resilient security posture for our global operations. You will manage the vulnerability lifecycle and triage security alerts to mitigate threats in real-time. By partnering with Infrastructure and Network teams, you will enhance Privileged Access Management (PAM) processes to protect our sensitive data. You will also develop and refine security runbooks and operational procedures to ensure consistent, repeatable security standards across all sites.   • Analyze logs and security events within platforms like Splunk to identify, triage, and escalate potential security incidents effectively.

Why Cisco?

We’ve been innovating fearlessly for 40 years to create solutions that power how humans and technology work together across the physical and digital worlds. These solutions provide customers with unparalleled security, visibility, and insights across the entire digital footprint.

Fueled by the depth and breadth of our technology, we experiment and create meaningful solutions. Add to that our worldwide network of doers and experts, and you’ll see that the opportunities to grow and build are limitless. We work as a team, collaborating with empathy to make really big things happen on a global scale. Because our solutions are everywhere, our impact is everywhere.

We are Cisco, and our power starts with you.

title: Writer and Editor
description:
About Us

At The Huntington, we believe that having a team of diverse backgrounds and voices working together will enable us to support and promote the appreciation of the humanities, the arts, and botanical science. The Huntington is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and is committed to providing employment opportunities regardless of race, religious creed, color, national origin, disability, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation or any other characteristic protected by local, state or federal law.

The Huntington

Founded in 1919, The Huntington is a collections-based research and educational institution open to the public, housing world-class library, art, and botanical collections. Its mission is to support research and promote education in the arts, humanities, and botanical science and to display and interpret its extraordinary resources for diverse audiences.

The Culture

Here we are committed to the highest of standards in all that we do – from preserving and protecting the collections, to exhibitions, educational and scholarly programming, visitor and reader services, and beyond. Achieving excellence across these pursuits requires a diversity of perspectives, expertise, experience, and methodologies.

At The Huntington, our organizational Culture is shaped by the following core values: Intellectual curiosity, Collaboration, Stewardship, Belonging, and Integrity.

  • Intellectual Curiosity: Knowledge, lifelong learning, and a spirit of inquiry are at the core of our mission and organizational culture.

  • Collaboration: Teamwork and a collaborative attitude are important at all levels of The Huntington. We foster relationships internally among our departments and externally with organizations throughout the community.

  • Stewardship: We are committed to the care and development of our collections, our financial and physical resources, our staff, and our community.

  • Belonging: We strive to attract and maintain a workforce of individuals with diverse talents, backgrounds, and perspectives. Our organizational culture promotes a sense of welcome, inclusion, and connection.

  • Integrity: We value respect and honesty, working to fulfill our mission with honor and ethical principles.

Job Description

About the Role

The Writer and Editor is a skilled storyteller and editor responsible for producing high-quality feature and narrative content and providing editorial support across Communications and Marketing. Reporting to the Director of News and Media Relations, this role helps execute institutional storytelling initiatives and ensures written materials meet The Huntington’s editorial standards.

This role requires a writer who is equally comfortable developing deeply reported features, producing high-quality editorial and marketing copy, and editing advertisements and events on deadline.

An integral member of the Office of Communications and Marketing, the Writer and Editor collaborates with colleagues across the institution to identify stories, develop content, and support the timely delivery of communications products. The Office of Communications and Marketing develops and amplifies The Huntington’s stories and storytellers across multiple channels—ensuring the institution’s work is accessible, relevant, and widely shared.

The position also serves as backup to the Senior Editor as assigned.

The successful candidate demonstrates an inclusive, collaborative approach and experience working with people from diverse racial, ethnic, geographic, and socioeconomic backgrounds.

This is a limited-term position, currently budgeted for one year.

Essential Duties

Editing & Editorial Support

  • Edits and proofreads a wide range of materials—including event materials, news releases, newsletters, announcements, reports, and marketing collateral—to ensure clarity, accuracy, consistency of tone, and adherence to AP style and The Huntington Editorial Style Guide.

  • Provides day-to-day editorial support across Communications and Marketing projects, maintaining quality and consistency across deliverables.

  • Serves as backup to the Senior Editor on assigned projects, helping maintain editorial workflows, version control, and production deadlines.

  • Supports the Director of News and Media Relations in executing editorial priorities and content initiatives.

Feature Writing & Content Development

  • Researches, develops, and writes compelling feature and narrative stories that highlight The Huntington’s collections, research, exhibitions, programs, and people.

  • Produces engaging content for print and digital platforms, including web features, blog posts, and institutional publications.

  • Identifies and pitches story ideas in collaboration with Communications & Marketing colleagues and subject-matter experts.

  • Conducts interviews and background research to support accurate, audience-focused storytelling.

  • Crafts clear, compelling marketing and advertising copy in support of exhibitions, programs, campaigns, and institutional initiatives.

Publications & Project Support

  • Supports production of major publications (including the Annual Report) by drafting and editing content, coordinating inputs, assisting with image selection, and partnering with design staff on layout and production.

  • Tracks project milestones and deadlines to support timely delivery of communications products.

  • Assists with adapting content for web and multi-channel distribution.

Team Collaboration

  • Participates in editorial planning meetings and content calendar discussions.

  • Builds productive working relationships across the institution to surface story opportunities.

  • Assists Communications & Marketing staff with editing and proofreading needs.

  • Provides updates on assigned projects and divisional activities.

Additional Responsibilities

  • Works occasional evenings and weekends as required to support events, deadlines, and institutional priorities.

  • Other duties as assigned.

Candidate Requirements and Experience

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

Required

  • Exceptional writing and storytelling skills with demonstrated strength in feature writing and line editing.

  • Strong editorial judgment and attention to detail.

  • Advanced working knowledge of AP style and institutional style standards.

  • Proactive mindset, with the ability to anticipate storytelling opportunities and independently surface strong story ideas.

  • Strategic thinking that connects writing and editing work to institutional priorities, audience engagement, and long-term visibility.

  • Systems thinking, including the ability to evaluate and improve workflows, processes, and operational systems to strengthen editorial efficiency and collaboration.

  • Demonstrated strength in project management, with the ability to manage multiple assignments, prioritize effectively, and consistently meet deadlines.

  • Demonstrated ability to write effective marketing and advertising copy aligned with institutional voice, brand standards, and audience goals.

  • Ability to maintain clear communication and seamless collaboration across teams and stakeholders.

  • Strong interviewing and interpersonal skills.

  • Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment.

  • Commitment to inclusive, accessible communications.

  • Proficiency with MS Office, SharePoint, Teams, Adobe, and collaborative editing tools

Preferred

  • Experience using project and workflow management tools (e.g., ClickUp, Asana, Monday, or similar) to track progress and support cross-team coordination.

  • Experience working with Digital Asset Management (DAM) systems, including uploading images and applying accurate keywords, metadata, rights information, and captions to support discoverability, accessibility, and proper asset governance.

Education and Experience

  • These skills and abilities are usually acquired through the completion of a B.A. degree, preferably in English, journalism, or equivalent coursework. Demonstrated ability and job experience may provide an appropriate substitute for preferred degree.

  • Five to seven years’ experience in editing and writing for cultural organizations, museums, universities, and/or news outlets.

Working Conditions

  • Primarily office-based with standard computer use.

  • Must be able to work some evenings and weekends as required by institutional events and deadlines.

Compensation & Benefits

We provide competitive compensation, generous benefits and perks for all eligible employees including:

  • Pay Range: $85,000.00-$90,000.00. Commensurate on experience.

  • Medical, Dental, Vision

  • 403(b) retirement plan and matching retirement plan with an outstanding employer match

  • Hybrid remote work schedule available for applicable positions

  • Considerable paid time off, including annual leave, sick leave, and holidays

  • Discounts for staff in The Huntington Store and restaurants

  • Free admission to various museums and cultural institutions

  • Free passes each month to welcome family and friends to visit the grounds

The Application Process

Please submit a cover letter, portfolio of published writing and resume. You will have the opportunity to submit additional documents in the “My Experience” section of the application.

In this role, you will be critical to the success of our production workforce by ensuring all Production Associates are fully trained, proficient, and compliant with all production processes and safety standards. Your primary responsibilities will be to deliver engaging and hands-on training, develop and maintain training content and work instructions, and continuously assess the effectiveness of the delivered training. You will work closely with Production Leadership and cross-functional teams (e.g., Engineering, Quality) to ensure training materials reflect the latest process improvements and quality standards.

Both day and night shifts are available.

What you'll do:

  • Training Delivery & Facilitation:

    • Conduct engaging, hands-on, and classroom-based training for new and current Production Associates on all standard operating procedures (SOPs), work instructions, and safety protocols.

    • Mentor and coach Production Associates on the floor to ensure proper technique, quality adherence, and efficient execution of tasks.

    • Coordinate training schedules with Production Supervisors and Leads to minimize impact on production goals.

  • Content Development & Maintenance:

    • Develop, write, and maintain clear, user-friendly, and technically accurate work instructions, SOPs, and visual aids (e.g., photos, videos) for all production processes.

    • Collaborate with Engineering, Quality, and Maintenance teams to capture and document process changes, updates, and improvements immediately upon implementation.

    • Ensure all training materials comply with company policies, safety regulations , and quality management systems.

  • Training Effectiveness & Improvement:

    • Develop and implement assessment tools (e.g., practical exams, written tests) to measure the effectiveness of training and ensure employee competency.

    • Track and report on employee training progress and certification status.

    • Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives by providing feedback on training content and delivery to enhance operational efficiency.

  • Safety & Compliance:

    • Ensure all training emphasizes a safety-first mindset and strict adherence to all OSHA and company safety policies.

    • Help identify potential hazards and train associates on appropriate preventative measures.

What you'll bring:

  • Experience:

    • Minimum of 2 years of experience in a manufacturing or production environment.

    • Proven experience in a training, mentoring, or instructional role, preferably on a factory floor.

    • Experience with developing and maintaining technical documentation (SOPs, Work Instructions).

  • Technical & Instructional Aptitude:

    • Strong technical aptitude with the ability to quickly learn and understand complex production processes and equipment.

    • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex concepts clearly and concisely to diverse audiences.

    • Familiarity with various training methodologies and adult learning principles.

  • Problem-Solving & Detail Orientation:

    • Strong organizational skills and exceptional attention to detail in documenting processes and tracking training data.

    • Ability to troubleshoot and resolve immediate training or content issues as they arise.

  • Interpersonal Skills:

    • Ability to work effectively and collaboratively with Production Associates, Leads , Supervisors , and cross-functional teams.

    • A positive and patient demeanor, committed to fostering a culture of continuous learning.

Where you'll work:

This role is based at Form Factory 1 in Weirton, WV—an easy commute from the city of Pittsburgh, PA. This 550,000-square-foot facility is our hub for high-volume battery production and a leader in the new era of American energy manufacturing.

title: On-Site Service Engineer - Data Center/ Server Hardware
location: Chicago, IL, United States of America
description:
What success looks like in this role:

Unisys Corporation is seeking an experienced On-Site Service Engineer (OSE) to provide hands-on support for enterprise data center servers and hardware environments, including next-generation AI infrastructure.

This is a hands-on server hardware and break/fix role. The successful candidate will have direct experience diagnosing, repairing, replacing, and maintaining enterprise server hardware in a data center, field service, or customer-facing environment.

Prior AI experience is not required. Strong experience with enterprise servers and data center hardware is the priority.

What You’ll Do

  • Provide on-site technical support for Dell PowerEdge and other enterprise server hardware
  • Diagnose and resolve server hardware failures and system issues to minimize customer downtime
  • Perform hands-on hardware installation, removal, replacement, and repair, including:
    • Memory/DIMMs
    • CPUs/processors
    • Power supplies
    • Fans and cooling components
    • Hard drives/SSDs
    • RAID/HBA components
    • NICs and other PCIe components
    • GPUs and accelerator hardware
    • Motherboards/system boards and other server components
  • Perform rack-and-stack, server installation, cabling, component swaps, and hardware configuration
  • Troubleshoot issues involving server hardware, BIOS/firmware, operating systems, and hardware diagnostics
  • Perform firmware and BIOS updates and utilize server management tools such as Dell iDRAC or comparable platforms
  • Execute both reactive break/fix and preventive maintenance following established procedures
  • Troubleshoot and isolate hardware failures using documented diagnostic procedures and technical resources
  • Work directly with customers and internal technical teams during service events to communicate status, troubleshoot issues, and drive resolution
  • Accurately document service activities, hardware replacements, troubleshooting steps, and resolution details
  • Escalate complex technical issues when appropriate

  • Participate in on-call rotations and provide extended coverage as required

You will be successful in this role if you have:

What You Bring – Required

  • 3+ years of hands-on experience supporting enterprise servers, data center hardware, or similar infrastructure
  • Direct, hands-on experience physically working on server hardware — installing, removing, diagnosing, repairing, or replacing server components
  • Experience troubleshooting and replacing components such as memory, CPUs, power supplies, storage, RAID/HBA, NICs, fans/cooling systems, PCIe components, or GPUs
  • Experience working with rack-mounted enterprise servers in a data center, field service, or customer environment
  • Strong understanding of server hardware architecture and troubleshooting methodology
  • Experience with hardware diagnostics, BIOS/firmware, and server management tools
  • Familiarity with Linux or similar operating systems
  • Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills with the ability to independently diagnose hardware issues
  • Comfortable working independently in a customer-facing environment
  • Ability to clearly communicate technical issues and resolutions to customers and internal teams
  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs., travel to customer sites, and support flexible/on-call schedules

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting Dell PowerEdge servers
  • Dell or other enterprise hardware certifications
  • Experience with iDRAC, iLO, or comparable server management platforms
  • Experience supporting GPU/AI server infrastructure
  • Experience with data center operations, rack/stack, structured cabling, or server deployment
  • Associate’s or Bachelor’s degree in IT, Computer Science, or a related field

Important Note

AI infrastructure experience is not required. Candidates with strong enterprise server and data center hardware experience who are willing to learn emerging AI platforms are encouraged to apply.

title: Software Engineer
description:
The application window is expected to close on: 09/11/2026

Job posting may be removed earlier if the position is filled or if a sufficient number of applications are received.

Meet the team

We are seeking an experienced and motivated Software Engineer to join our Service Provider High End Router (Cisco 8000) team within the R&D department, contributing to the evolution of next-generation networking products! In this role, you’ll develop and optimize firmware, SDKs, simulators, and compilers for Cisco Silicon One™ architecture, with a strong focus on using the power of P4 (Programming Protocol-Independent Packet Processors). This is a phenomenal opportunity to work with pioneering technology that’s shaping the future of networking!

You’ll be part of a diverse team dedicated to delivering innovative, high-quality solutions on Cisco 8000, featuring the latest Silicon One ASICs. You will play a key role in developing the SDK and/or control plane for networking protocols, collaborating with talented colleagues to drive industry-leading advancements. Join us and be a part of something outstanding!

Your impact

As a Software Engineer, you will design and develop a broad set of advanced networking features. With the foundational capabilities of our next‑generation platforms already established, this role offers a true ground‑floor opportunity to drive the next phase of product growth. You will help shape our convergence strategy in the Service Provider space and deliver high‑impact features powering Web, Cloud, Data Center, and Mobile networking solutions.

  • Design, implement, and test C, C++, and P4 programs to define packet‑processing behaviors on high‑performance network devices.

  • Build, optimize, and enhance the backend of the P4 compiler to fully leverage the capabilities of advanced networking hardware.

  • Solve complex resource‑management challenges and optimize resource allocation across programmable network‑processing pipelines.

  • Collaborate closely with ASIC engineers to ensure seamless integration of P4 programs with next‑generation IC designs, including providing compiler support throughout hardware development cycles.

  • Participate in the design and implementation of new C, C++, and P4 language features to support the evolving needs of network application developers.

  • Develop Python‑based test frameworks and author Python test cases to validate SDK functionality and ensure correctness, performance, and reliability of P4‑based data‑plane programming.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree with 5+ years of relevant experience or master's degree with 3+ years of relevant experience.

  • Experience in software design and development using C, C++, or P4, including contributions to production‑quality systems.

  • Experience in troubleshooting, debugging, and resolving sophisticated software issues across large, distributed codebases, with practical experience in using tools such as GDB, PDB, etc.

  • Experience with Layer 2 (L2) and Layer 3 (L3) networking technologies, protocols, and data‑plane behaviors.

  • Experience in Python with the ability to develop scalable, maintainable, and production-ready software solutions.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with network‑processor software programming is a strong plus.

Why Cisco?

At Cisco, we’re revolutionizing how data and infrastructure connect and protect organizations in the AI era – and beyond. We’ve been innovating fearlessly for 40 years to create solutions that power how humans and technology work together across the physical and digital worlds. These solutions provide customers with unparalleled security, visibility, and insights across the entire digital footprint.

Fueled by the depth and breadth of our technology, we experiment and create meaningful solutions. Add to that our worldwide network of doers and experts, and you’ll see that the opportunities to grow and build are limitless. We work as a team, collaborating with empathy to make really big things happen on a global scale. Because our solutions are everywhere, our impact is everywhere.

We are Cisco, and our power starts with you.

  • Good skills in embedded systems, cloud environments, web applications and mobile applications preferred.

title: Legal Intern
description:

title: Night Auditor
description:
The Night Auditor is responsible for ensuring the hotel’s operational and financial continuity during the night shift, combining excellence in guest service with accuracy in accounting and auditing processes.

He or she acts as the main representative of the Front Office in the absence of the Night Manager during the night, ensuring a safe and seamless experience aligned with the hotel’s luxury standards, while correctly executing the daily financial closing.

Responsibilities

Guest Service and Night Operations

  • Welcomes, registers, and bids farewell to guests during the night shift, ensuring professional, warm, and efficient service.

  • Acts as the main point of contact for guests overnight, handling requests, concerns, and special situations with autonomy and sound judgment.

  • Resolves complaints and sensitive situations in accordance with established protocols, escalating to management when necessary.

  • Ensures a safe, calm, and comfortable environment in public areas and the lobby during the shift.

  • Promotes and performs upselling of rooms and hotel services when operations allow.

Night Audit and Financial Control

  • Fully and accurately executes all night audit and daily closing procedures.

  • Reviews rates, routings, taxes, charges, and transactions to ensure financial integrity.

  • Performs cash reconciliations, fund balancing, and cash control in accordance with Finance department standards.

  • Generates and distributes nightly financial and operational reports within established deadlines.

  • Identifies discrepancies, errors, or process deviations and reports them in a timely manner.

Operations and Security

  • Oversees lobby and public area activity during the night shift, ensuring order and compliance with standards.

  • Coordinates with Security and Maintenance regarding any technical issues or risk situations.

  • Actively participates in emergency management in accordance with the hotel’s emergency response plan.

  • Controls access and manages the issuance and safekeeping of master keys when required.

Operational Coordination and Continuity

  • Reviews next-day arrivals, departures, and requests, ensuring information is updated in the PMS.

  • Ensures proper preparation of VIP reservations, late arrivals, and special profiles.

  • Maintains structured and detailed communication with the day shift through clear incident reports and follow-up notes.

  • Ensures accurate updating of guest profiles and comments in the hotel management system.

Representation and Night Leadership

  • Represents the Front Office during the night shift in the absence of management.

  • Supports the training of new team members in audit procedures and night service standards when required.

  • Leads by example, conveying professionalism, composure, and a strong service orientation.

Education

  • Studies in tourism, hospitality, or business administration are considered an asset.

Experience

  • Previous experience in Front Office or Night Audit, preferably in 4- or 5-star hotels.

  • Experience with PMS (Opera or similar systems).

  • Knowledge of basic accounting processes and cash handling.

Competencies

  • High level of accuracy and attention to detail.

  • Ability to work independently and make decisions under pressure.

  • Excellent interpersonal communication skills.

  • Strong discipline in handling cash and financial procedures.

  • Service-oriented mindset with the ability to anticipate guest needs.

  • Proficiency in English; additional languages are an asset.

  • Category B driving license.

Candidate must be a citizen of the European Union or possess a valid work permit for Spain.

title: Director of Operations Fellow
description:
At Uncommon Schools, we know running exceptional schools takes more than great
instruction—it also takes exemplary operations! Uncommon Schools' operations leaders work
passionately to ensure that our faculty maximizes time and energy on student achievement.
They design, implement, and refine systems that anticipate the needs of the school community.
As service-oriented leaders, they tackle problems, share standard methodologies across
campuses, and respond to urgent needs. They partner to build an academic and cultural
environment that supports our ultimate goal: ensuring that every student will earn a college
degree.

The Director of Operations Fellow is a full-time position that prepares you to become a Director
of Operations (DOO) of an Uncommon school. As DOO, you will lead a school in partnership
with the Principal, working together to ensure your students receive an exemplary education.

The DOO Fellowship is based on a foundation of four core elements that are aligned to the
competencies of Uncommon leaders. Each element is designed to build Fellows’ capacity
towards becoming effective DOOs. These include Professional Development, Experiential
Learning, Practical Application and Reflective Practice.

The DOO Fellowship typically lasts one year; however, the length of time will vary based on
open positions and DOO Fellow readiness. Fellows should expect to work in multiple locations
and gradespans within the region. Fellow placement is based on the region’s needs as well as
Fellows’ growth areas and matching them with host DOOs to best support their development.

Professional Development

All Fellows will attend a series of professional development workshops throughout the
Fellowship. The subject matter of these workshops is grounded in the leadership competencies
that DOOs are evaluated and developed on.

Experiential Learning

Feedback and coaching, especially when individualized, are critical tools that will support the
Fellow’s growth as a leader. Fellows will engage in experiential learning activities, and receive
feedback targeted at their individualized areas of growth. Experiential learning activities include:
submission of weekly deliverables; on-site coaching with real-time feedback; and practice clinics
where fellows will engage in case studies, role plays, and problem solving exercises.

Practical Application

Fellows are placed at an existing Uncommon school and serve as full-time members of the
school's operations team. They engage in operations work at their host school, tackle school or
regional-based operations projects, and conduct observations and analysis of operational
systems. Fellows are responsible for completing a variety of pre-determined deliverables that
expose them to all of the key components of DOO work. Practical application includes an
Immersion in which the Fellow acts as DOO in place of their host DOO for 4-6 weeks. During
this time, their host DOO is offsite and the Fellow is acting DOO and co-leads the school
alongside the Principal.

Reflective Discourse

The Fellowship will create space at in-person sessions for reflective discourse, so that Fellows
can learn from their own experiences and those of others in the cohort. Fellows will also be
supported in developing a reflective practice, where they will codify their learning through written
reflections and create plans to make their growth and development actionable.

  • Passionate commitment to the mission of Uncommon Schools;
  • Passionate commitment to improve the minds, characters, and lives of students both in and out of school;
  • Ability to strategically manage and prioritize time and tasks effectively to fully meet the needs of their school, with a lens towards systems thinking;
  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment; flexible, able to work autonomously as well as take direction as needed;
  • Comfort with managing ambiguous situations and moving to clarity/solution;
  • Ability to learn something new and/or “do what it takes” to ensure the school receives high-quality operations despite obstacles;
  • Proactive, strategic problem-solver who is able to work successfully in a fast-paced environment, often while balancing competing priorities;
  • High-quality communication and relationship-building skills with multiple partners including teachers, students, families, vendors, and colleagues;
  • Ability to have difficult conversations in a respectful manner;
  • Excellent computer skills, including Microsoft Office, Word, Excel and Access;
  • Dedication to self-reflection and continual professional growth; approaches every experience as a chance to learn and grow and understands that introspection and the outward expression of that learning is essential to leadership;
  • School-based or other educational experience preferred;
  • Required experience:
    • 4 or more years of work experience;
    • At least 1 year of experience in operations leadership (experience in K-12 school operations is preferred)
    • At least 1 year of experience coaching, leading, and/or managing others (e.g., Special Projects Manager, Associate Director of Operations, Instructional Leader, or other equivalent experience);
    • Project planning experience, with proven ability to see large projects through to completion;
    • A Bachelor’s degree.

title: Occupancy and Inspection Specialist
description:
Position Summary:

The Occupancy and Inspection Specialist administers key functions of the Housing Choice Voucher (Section 8) Program, including participant eligibility, rent calculations, case management, housing inspections, and regulatory compliance. This position works with participants and property owners to ensure program requirements are met and housing units comply with applicable HUD standards and DCMHA policies.

Job responsibilities may include but are not limited to:

Housing Inspection and Unit Compliance

  • Conduct required housing inspections, including initial, annual/periodic, special, emergency, complaint, and re-inspections, in accordance with applicable HUD inspection requirements and DCMHA policies.
  • Evaluate housing units for compliance with applicable HUD health, safety, and housing quality requirements.
  • Accurately document inspection findings and maintain required inspection records.
  • Prepare and issue notices identifying deficiencies, required corrective actions, and applicable compliance deadlines.
  • Conduct follow-up inspections to verify completion of required repairs and corrective actions.
  • Coordinate enforcement actions associated with failed inspections, including appropriate notices, abatements, contract actions, and program termination processes in accordance with HUD requirements and DCMHA policy.
  • Communicate inspection requirements, results, and corrective actions to property owners, landlords, participants, and other appropriate parties.
  • Schedule and coordinate inspections to meet applicable HUD and agency timelines.
  • Maintain accurate inspection documentation and rent reasonableness records.
  • Identify and report health, safety, or other potentially hazardous conditions encountered during inspections.
  • Follow established safety procedures when entering and inspecting residential properties.

Occupancy, Eligibility, and Case Management

  • Manage an assigned Housing Choice Voucher caseload in accordance with HUD regulations, the DCMHA Administrative Plan, and established agency procedures.
  • Process applicant admissions, annual/periodic reexaminations, interim reexaminations, household composition changes, income changes, and other required participant actions.
  • Obtain, review, and verify household income, assets, deductions, family composition, citizenship/eligible immigration status, and other eligibility information using HUD-approved verification methods.
  • Utilize HUD's Enterprise Income Verification (EIV) system and other authorized verification resources.
  • Calculate Total Tenant Payment (TTP), tenant rent, utility allowances, Housing Assistance Payments (HAP), and other applicable amounts accurately and timely.
  • Prepare, review, and submit HUD-50058 transactions and related documentation.
  • Prepare and maintain Housing Assistance Payment contracts and associated participant and owner records.
  • Identify, research, document, and resolve EIV discrepancies, unreported income, overpayments, underpayments, and other program discrepancies.
  • Establish and monitor repayment agreements when required by applicable regulations and agency policy.
  • Process moves, portability actions, terminations, and other participant changes in accordance with program requirements.
  • Receive and process reasonable accommodation and modification requests in accordance with the Fair Housing Act, Section 504, the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), and applicable agency procedures.
  • Maintain participant confidentiality and safeguard personally identifiable and sensitive information.

III. Program Compliance, Operational, and Field Support

  • Maintain complete, accurate, organized, and audit-ready participant, owner, and inspection files.
  • Enter and maintain accurate information within applicable housing management, HUD, and agency systems.
  • Monitor caseload and inspection deadlines to ensure timely completion of inspections, reexaminations, certifications, notices, and HUD submissions.
  • Participate in internal quality-control reviews, SEMAP reviews, audits, HUD monitoring, State monitoring, and other compliance activities as required.
  • Research and correct file, system, or documentation deficiencies identified through internal or external reviews.
  • Respond to inquiries from applicants, participants, landlords, property owners, and other stakeholders in a professional, respectful, and timely manner.
  • Explain program requirements, participant responsibilities, landlord responsibilities, inspection requirements, and applicable agency procedures.
  • Maintain professional boundaries and confidentiality when working with applicants, participants, property owners, and members of the public.
  • Operate agency vehicles safely and in accordance with agency vehicle and safety policies.
  • Travel throughout the service area to conduct inspections, meetings, training, and other assigned program activities.
  • Attend required HUD, fair housing, inspection, safety, and program-related training.
  • Perform other duties assigned that are consistent with the purpose and responsibilities of the position.

Qualifications:

  • High school diploma or G.E.D. equivalent.
  • Minimum 2 years experience in performing administrative, eligibility, housing, property inspection, compliance, case management, customer service, or similarly detailed work.
  • Experience working with confidential records and performing accurate data entry and documentation.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Associate degree or higher in public administration, business administration, social services, housing, property management, construction/building technology, or a related field.
  • Previous experience with a Public Housing Agency, Housing Choice Voucher Program, affordable housing program, property management organization, or other federally funded program.
  • Experience conducting residential property or housing inspections.
  • Experience with HUD systems, EIV, HUD-50058 processing, rent calculations, or housing management software.
  • HUD HCV occupancy, eligibility, rent calculation, or inspection-related certification or training.

Competencies, Knowledge, and Abilities:

  • Knowledge of, or ability to learn, HUD Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) regulations, housing inspection standards, and agency policies and procedures.
  • Knowledge of eligibility determination, income verification, rent calculations, EIV, HUD-50058 reporting, and related program requirements.
  • General knowledge of Fair Housing, ADA/Section 504, reasonable accommodation, and confidentiality requirements.
  • Strong organizational and time-management skills with the ability to manage a caseload, inspections, and multiple regulatory deadlines.
  • Strong attention to detail with the ability to maintain accurate, complete, and audit-ready records.
  • Ability to interpret and consistently apply regulations, policies, and program requirements.
  • Effective written and verbal communication, customer service, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to communicate professionally with participants, property owners, landlords, coworkers, and community partners.
  • Proficiency with computers, electronic records, Microsoft Office, data entry, and housing management systems.
  • Ability to work independently in both office and field environments while exercising sound judgment.
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and appropriately handle sensitive participant and program information.
  • Ability to successfully complete required HUD, housing inspection, program, and safety-related training.

Pre-hire: Mandatory drug testing and background check.

title: Clinical Trainer and Auditor - Utilization Management Experience - Remote-AZ
description:
Awarded a Healthiest Employer, Blue Cross Blue Shield of Arizona aims to fulfill its mission to inspire health and make it easy. AZ Blue offers a variety of health insurance products and services to meet the diverse needs of individuals, families, and small and large businesses as well as providing information and tools to help individuals make better health decisions.

At AZ Blue, we have a hybrid workforce strategy, called Workability, that offers flexibility with how and where employees work. Our positions are classified as hybrid, onsite or remote. While the majority of our employees are hybrid, the following classifications drive our current minimum onsite requirements:

  • Hybrid People Leaders: must reside in AZ, required to be onsite at least twice per week

  • Hybrid Individual Contributors: must reside in AZ, unless otherwise cited within this posting, required to be onsite at least once per week

  • Hybrid 2 (Operational Roles such as but not limited to: Customer Service, Claims Processors, and Correspondence positions): must reside in AZ, unless otherwise cited within this posting, required to be onsite at least once per month

  • Onsite: daily onsite requirement based on the essential functions of the job

  • Remote: not held to onsite requirements, however, leadership can request presence onsite for business reasons including but not limited to staff meetings, one-on-ones, training, and team building

Please note that onsite requirements may change in the future, based on business need, and job responsibilities. Most employees should expect onsite requirements and at a minimum of once per week.

This remote work opportunity requires residency, and work to be performed, within the State of Arizona.

PURPOSE OF THE JOB

  • Responsible for designing, delivering, and evaluating clinical training programs and audit activities that promote standardized clinical decision-making, regulatory compliance and quality improvement across Utilization Management and Care Management initiatives.
  • This role supports staff development, onboarding, inter-rater reliability, and ongoing education for clinical teams to enhance performance, operational consistency, and achievement of organizational goals and initiatives.

QUALIFICATIONS

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

Required Work Experience

  • 5 years of direct clinical care experience in a healthcare setting
  • 2 years of experience in Utilization Management, Care Management, Health Management, Disease Management, or other managed care operations.
  • 4 years of experience in clinical training, education, auditing, or quality improvement, preferably in managed care.

Required Education

  • Associate degree in general field of study or Post High School Nursing Diploma

Required Licenses

  • Active, current, and unrestricted license to practice in the State of Arizona (a state in the United States) (or an endorsement to work in Arizona) as a behavioral health professional such as LCSW, LPC, LISAC, LMFT, or licensed psychologist (Psy.D. or Ph.D.),or RDN (Registered Dietitian Nutritionist), CDCES (Certified Diabetes Care and Education Specialist), OR an active, current, and unrestricted license to practice nursing in either the State of Arizona or another state in the United States recognized by the Nursing Licensure Compact (NLC) as an RN, OR an active, current, and unrestricted license to practice in the State of Arizona as an LPN.

Required Certifications

  • N/A

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

Preferred Work Experience

  • 5 years of experience in clinical education, training, auditing, quality improvement, and instructional design in either Utilization Management or Case Management.
  • 1 year of experience working with Milliman Care Guidelines (MCG), and / or other clinical criteria/guidelines.
  • Experience conducting clinical audits, quality reviews, or inter-rater reliability assessments related to evidence- based clinical decision making, documentation accuracy, and regulatory or accreditation standards.
  • Experience supporting onboarding, staff development, remediation, or performance improvement initiatives for clinical staff.

Preferred Education

  • Master’s degree in nursing, Master of Science, Social Work, Behavioral Health, Psychology, or another related clinical field.

Preferred Certifications

  • Active and current certifications such as: Certified Case Manager (CCM), Certified Professional in Healthcare Quality (CPHQ), Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA), or a Utilization Management Certification related to evidence-based clinical criteria such as MCG.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Develop and deliver training and education for clinical staff on clinical philosophy, evidence-based practice, documentation standards, regulatory requirements, and operational workflows related to Utilization Management, Care Management and Health Management.
  • Assess and prioritize training needs based on workflow changes, audit findings, stakeholder feedback, business priorities, and staff readiness.
  • Evaluate training effectiveness using feedback, knowledge checks, audit trends, and performance data to identify gaps and recommend improvements.
  • Assist with the development and evaluation of performance goals, quality management activities, and improvement initiatives that support clinical, operational, and regulatory standards.
  • Coordinate onboarding and training readiness activities, including system access, required resources, non-clinical checklists, and resolution of technical barriers.
  • Perform quality audits for Utilization Management activities and medical director determinations to evaluate consistency, accuracy, and compliance in evidence-based clinical decision-making, including inter-rater reliability assessments for Utilization Management as applicable. Audit activities assess whether medical director’s determinations are clear, concise, and documented to support clinical reviewers’ understanding and next-step action.
  • Perform quality audits for Care Management and Health Management activities to assess accuracy and completeness of documentation, alignment of interventions with care plans, and progression toward member outcomes and goals.
  • Support targeted education, remediation, and performance improvement initiatives based on audit findings, operational needs, and quality management priorities.
  • Support process improvement initiatives by providing education, workflow guidance, and technical application support to clinical staff and stakeholders.
  • Facilitate calibration and standardization activities to support consistent application of clinical criteria, policies, workflows, and documentation expectations.
  • Present case status updates and relevant findings to the manager, supervisor, and when indicated, the medical director to support clinical oversight, decision making, and appropriate follow-up.
  • Assist with the review, revision, and ongoing maintenance of policies and procedures to ensure alignment with regulatory requirements, organizational standards, and evidence-based clinical practice.
  • Assist with ad hoc training assignments and educational initiatives as needed to support departmental priorities, workflow changes, and staff development.
  • Maintain compliance with applicable state, federal, AZ Blue, URAC, CMS and other regulatory and accreditation standards.
  • Maintain complete, accurate, and timely records in accordance with department policies, procedures, and documentation standards.
  • Participate in continuing education and remain current on developments in clinical practice, medicine, managed care, and applicable regulatory requirements.
  • Facilitate hands-on technical training for Care Management, Health Management, and Utilization Management workflows, including system navigation, documentation expectations, authorization entry, assessment completion, mock scenarios, and guided practice.
  • Develop training plans with learning objectives, workflow scenarios, guided practice, competency checks, and follow up coaching to support readiness for independent work.
  • Develop, maintain, version control for training materials, job aids, facilitator guides, and workflow resources to ensure accuracy, consistency, and alignment with current standards.
  • Coordinate cross-functional support between IT, new hires, and operational teams to address system access and application issues.
  • Facilitate structured onboarding using non-clinical checklists to ensure all requirements are completed.
  • Ensure system access readiness by validating functionality, conducting required testing, and verifying availability of tools and resources.
  • Utilize training environments to reinforce system proficiency through structured practice, guided navigation exercises, mock scenarios, and hands-on demonstrations of CM, HM, and UM workflows, including assessment completion and authorization entry.
  • The position requires a full-time work schedule. Full-time is defined as working at least 40 hours per week, plus any additional hours as requested or as needed to meet business requirements.
  • Perform all other duties as assigned.

COMPETENCIES

REQUIRED COMPETENCIES

Required Job Skills

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills. Excellent organizational skills and strong attention to detail
  • Possess proficient computer and technological skills especially Word, Excel, PowerPoint, SharePoint, Microsoft Teams/Webinar, and Internet
  • Ability to gather, analyze data and prepare informative and accurate reports.
  • Ability to understand the workflow of multiple components of the company and to assist in the creation and implementation of integrated policies, procedures, workplans and creative solutions.

Required Professional Competencies

  • Ability to develop, organize, motivate, coordinate, and collaborate effectively with stakeholders from multiple business areas across the organization.
  • Ability to successfully function in an environment characterized by risk taking, rapidly changing market conditions, strong competition and restructuring.
  • Strong understanding of the costs/quality challenges of today’s health care environment.
  • Knowledge of health and/or patient education and behavior change techniques.
  • Organizational skills to analyze, interpret data, synthesize, evaluate and explain educational concepts, practices and methodologies to staff and transfer data to and from written and verbal medium.
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and privacy
  • Advanced knowledge of Adult Learning Theory principles and demonstrated ability to facilitate training that resonates with all learning styles
  • Demonstrate strong interpersonal and active listening skills
  • Demonstrated organizational skills with the ability to priortize tasks and work with multiple priorities
  • Follow and accept instruction and direction
  • Establish and maintain working relationships in a collaborative team environment
  • Apply independent and sound judgment with good problem solving skilll

Required Leadership Experience and Competencies

  • Desire and capability to drive toward and achieve high standard of quality and results.
  • Mindset geared toward the creation, execution and continuous improvement of clinical benefit management department and programs. Intellectual curiosity and ability to view old problems/issues with a fresh perspective.
  • Ability to perform job duties independently.
  • Ability to professionally represent AZ Blue in the community

PREFERRED COMPETENCIES

Preferred Job Skills

  • Advanced PC proficiency
  • Knowledge of CPT/HCPCs and ICD-10 coding

Preferred Professional Competencies

  • Knowledge of managed care, utilization management, and quality management

Preferred Leadership Experience and Competencies

  • N/A

Our Commitment

title: Founding Technical Product Manager
description:
About Us

At FurtherAI, we're building the AI agents that run insurance - a trillion-dollar industry still powered by manual work. By combining frontier agentic AI with deep domain expertise, we're reshaping how the industry's most critical work gets done.

We've raised more than $30M from top investors (Andreessen Horowitz, YC, Nexus, South Park Commons, Converge), grown more than 10x in the last 12 months, and work with some of the largest names in insurance - top 10 carriers/brokers, F100 & public companies.

We are a deeply technical company. Both founders are engineers, and engineers have an outsized say on product direction.

Now, we're looking for our first product hire - a Founding Product Manager to own product alongside the founders, define what we build, and build the product function from the ground up.

Why Join Us

  • Outsized ambition: We're out to build the definitive AI company for insurance - and we're moving faster than anyone in the space.

  • Own the product function: You're our first PM. You'll set how we scope, decide, and ship - and grow the team beneath you as we scale.

  • Elite team: Founders and engineers from the best companies and schools in the world - ex-Apple AI Research, Brex, Coinbase, and Uber; 4 YC founders and 6 ex-founders; grads of Stanford, Berkeley, IITs, and Cornell.

  • Massive market impact: Insurance is the backbone of global commerce. Our work reshapes how the industry operates.

What You'll Do

  • Be our first product hire. Define what product means at FurtherAI: how we scope, decide, and ship - and grow the team beneath you as we scale.

  • Own product direction with the founders. Shape where the product goes, then turn that vision into a plan the team can build - from the first insight to the shipped feature and everything after.

  • Define the future of AI in insurance. Decide how our agents behave - what they automate, which tools they use, where a human stays in the loop - for the workflows that run a trillion-dollar industry.

  • Go deep on how insurance actually works. Sit with brokers, underwriters, and carriers, find the real pain, and turn messy real-world workflows into product that feels obvious.

  • Keep us building the right thing, fast. Make sure the team always has high-impact, well-scoped work ahead of it, and define what "great" looks like before we build it.

  • Set the bar for quality and taste across everything we ship.

Representative Projects

  • The Universal Assistant. One place an insurance professional can ask for anything - "pull this broker's loss history, check it against our guidelines, draft the quote" - and watch an agent read the documents, pull from their systems, and do it end to end. You'll define what it can do and how people come to trust it.

  • Let anyone build an agent. Today, building an automation takes an engineer. You'll shape the product that lets an underwriter describe what they want in plain English and get back a working, reliable agent - the shift that turns FurtherAI from a tool into a platform.

  • Agents that work a case for days. An agent that emails a broker for a missing document, waits, follows up by phone, and picks the case back up when the reply lands. You'll invent what it means to hand a multi-day, multi-channel job to an agent - and supervise it like a teammate.

  • Agents that get better on their own. Workflows that learn from every run, catch where they went wrong, and improve without an engineer touching them. You'll define what "self-improving" means in a product people bet real money on.

What We're Looking For

  • 5+ years in product, much of it at early-stage / high-growth companies where you steered direction.

  • A track record shipping products that transform real professional workflows in complex domains.

  • Technical enough to earn engineers' trust - you reason fluently about agents and LLMs, prototype your ideas, and genuinely appreciate engineering tradeoffs. (You don't need to have shipped production code, but you're never hand-wavy.)

  • Deep intuition for LLMs and real excitement for turning AI capability into product people trust.

  • Strong discovery instincts - you tell stated needs from actual requirements, and define problems amid ambiguity without complete information.

  • Excellent written communication - you distill complexity into crisp, buildable specs.

  • Builder mentality - outcomes over process, high ownership. You're accountable for what ships, not just what you hand off.

Nice to Have

  • Insurance, reinsurance, or financial services background.

  • Built a product from 0→1 and stood up the processes around it.

  • Experience with integration-first products embedded inside customers' existing tools.

  • Comfort running your own quantitative analyses.

At FurtherAI, we set a high bar. We're not looking for someone who just wants a job - we're looking for someone who wants to build something transformative and own a big piece of it. If you thrive where the pace is fast, expectations are high, and the rewards are outsized, you'll love it here.

Benefits

  • Fully covered, best-in-class health, dental, and vision

  • Competitive compensation, meaningful stock options, company 401(k)

  • Unlimited PTO

  • Outstanding in-office culture in the heart of San Francisco

  • Lunch and dinner onsite

  • Team events - happy hours and off-sites

  • Pre-tax commuter benefits

Location: Manassas, VA
100% Onsite

The employee is occasionally required to stand, walk, reach with arms and hands, bend or twist, and to stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl. Vision abilities required by this job include close vision.

title: Business Systems Analyst
description:

The ideal candidate is a proactive, detail-oriented professional who excels in a business-facing operational environment. title: DSCA Duty Desk Officer
description:
BryceTech is seeking a DSCA Duty Desk Officer to support the National Guard Bureau (NGB) Domestic Operations (DOMOPS) mission. This position will provide operational support for Defense Support of Civil Authorities (DSCA) activities, including monitoring current operations, maintaining situational awareness, coordinating operational reporting, and supporting response activities during domestic incidents and emergencies.

The DSCA Duty Desk Officer will operate within a mission-focused current operations environment, supporting 24/7 operational awareness and coordination requirements. The position will monitor ongoing and emerging domestic events, synchronize information from multiple sources, prepare operational updates, and support communication between NGB, National Guard organizations, Department of Defense components, federal agencies, and other mission partners.

The ideal candidate will have experience supporting military operations, emergency management, operations centers, watch floors, or crisis response environments, with a strong understanding of DSCA processes and domestic response operations.

Key Responsibilities

  • Monitor and maintain situational awareness of domestic operations, incidents, and emerging mission requirements
  • Support 24/7 current operations activities, including watch floor operations, operational tracking, and incident reporting
  • Receive, analyze, and disseminate operational information from military, federal, state, territorial, and emergency management partners
  • Prepare operational summaries, situation reports (SITREPs), briefings, and other mission update products
  • Track DSCA requests, operational activities, response actions, and mission status updates
  • Support coordination and communication between NGB, National Guard units, DoD organizations, and interagency partners
  • Identify emerging issues, operational impacts, and resource requirements and elevate information to appropriate leadership
  • Maintain accurate operational records, logs, and documentation of current events and mission activities
  • Support incident response coordination during domestic emergencies, disasters, and contingency operations
  • Assist with preparation and execution of operational briefings, update meetings, and leadership engagements
  • Support continuity operations, mission assurance, and operational readiness activities
  • Assist with exercise support, operational planning events, and after-action reviews
  • Provide operational input for improving procedures, processes, and response coordination activities
  • Support development and maintenance of standard operating procedures, desk guides, and operational checklists
  • Coordinate information flow across multiple stakeholders to ensure timely and accurate reporting

Required Qualifications

  • Active Top Secret security clearance with SCI eligibility (TS/SCI)
  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in emergency management, homeland security, national security, military studies, public administration, or related discipline
  • 7+ years of experience supporting military operations, emergency management, homeland defense, or disaster response missions
  • Experience supporting operations centers, watch floors, command centers, or similar mission environments
  • Experience developing operational reports, briefings, and situational awareness products
  • Understanding of Defense Support of Civil Authorities (DSCA) processes and domestic response operations
  • Experience coordinating with military organizations, government agencies, or emergency management partners
  • Ability to analyze information quickly and provide accurate operational updates in a fast-paced environment
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills

Preferred Qualifications

  • Prior military experience, particularly within operations, plans, emergency management, or command center environments
  • Experience supporting National Guard Bureau, U.S. Northern Command (USNORTHCOM), Joint Staff, FEMA, DHS, or similar organizations
  • Experience serving as a Current Operations Officer, JOC Watch Officer, Battle Captain, Crisis Action Team member, or Emergency Operations Center staff member
  • Experience supporting large-scale domestic response operations, including natural disasters, civil emergencies, or national-level events
  • Familiarity with National Guard emergency response authorities and DSCA mission requirements
  • Experience supporting operational planning, exercises, and readiness assessments
  • Professional military education or equivalent operational training

Desired Certifications / Training

  • Incident Command System (ICS) training
  • National Incident Management System (NIMS) training
  • Emergency Operations Center (EOC) experience
  • Joint Professional Military Education (JPME)
  • Certified Emergency Manager (CEM)
  • Project Management Professional (PMP)
  • FEMA Master Continuity Practitioner (MCP)

Position is contingent upon contract award.

BryceTech offers a full range of benefits, including competitive salary, a comprehensive health plan including dental and vision coverage, company-paid life & disability insurance policies, 401(k) plan with company match, and an educational reimbursement program.

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

description:
About Samsung Austin Semiconductor
Samsung is a world leader in advanced semiconductor technology, founded on the belief that the pursuit of excellence creates a better world. At Samsung Austin Semiconductor, we are Innovating Today to Power the Devices of Tomorrow.

Come innovate with us!

Position Summary

The Infra Electrical Projects Team is seeking an Electrical Engineer to develop and execute CAPEX roadmaps for our critical electrical infrastructure. In this role, you will lead end-of-life retrofits and capacity expansion projects essential to sustaining the growth and reliability of our 24x7x365 semiconductor fabrication facilities. You will ensure that our power distribution systems are scalable, safe, and resilient to support world-class manufacturing.

Role and Responsibilities

Here’s What You’ll Be Responsible For:

  • Lead the design, code compliance, and safety validation for power distribution systems, ensuring peak equipment performance.

  • Oversee the full project lifecycle—from planning and conceptual design to execution and delivery—ensuring strict alignment with scope, schedule, and budget.

  • Develop, review, and approve site-wide electrical specifications for medium-voltage (MV) and low-voltage (LV) distribution equipment.

  • Author Feasibility Reports and Conceptual Designs for new Capital Investment Projects (CIP) and R&M (Repair & Maintenance) expense projects.

  • Provide expert engineering support during pre-construction, construction, and the final turnover to Operations.

  • Manage day-to-day activities of external consultant design teams, general contractors, and subcontractors for new builds and retrofit projects.

  • Develop comprehensive and accurate sequences of operations for all newly designed systems.

  • Apply and maintain industry standards, including SEMI F47 for voltage sag ride-through, to ensure facility uptime.

  • Perform Arc-Flash analysis and maintain site-wide compliance with code.

  • Proactively monitor and ensure the uptime and performance of the site’s power systems.

  • Perform QA/QC reviews on all engineering deliverables and vendor proposals.

  • Lead participation in internal and external ISO 50001 audits and drive the company’s corporate sustainability and energy-efficiency goals.

  • Partner with Project Managers, field technicians, and diverse stakeholders to solve complex infrastructure challenges.

Skills and Qualifications

Here's what you'll need:

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering from an ABET-accredited institution.

  • Minimum of 2+ years of electrical design or project experience within an industrial setting.

  • Experience with the design, sizing, and operation of Motor Control Centers (MCCs), ATS, STS, Transformers, Emergency Generators, and Uninterruptible Power Supplies (UPS).

  • Proficiency in electrical modeling software (e.g., ETAP, SKM)

  • Proven experience managing projects from design and specification through construction administration.

  • Ability to interpret complex design plans and shop drawings and conduct rigorous field reviews of work-in-progress.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present technical content clearly to various organizations.

  • Strong creative problem-solving skills, leadership potential, and a drive to meet aggressive goals within tight timelines.

title: New Grad RN Surgical Float Pool
description:
Job Description:

The Nursing Graduate works under the direct line-of-sight supervision of the Registered Nurse (RN) in the clinical setting and participates appropriately in the patient care delivery process. The incumbent also orients to the RN assignment, excluding independent nursing care. This position may participate in medication administration under the direction and supervision of the licensed RN.

The Nursing Graduate job can be utilized for up to 12 weeks while employees are in the Intermountain Nurse Residency program and are working toward preparing, testing, and passing the State Boards examination (obtaining an RN license). After that 12-week period, or if the Nursing Graduate fails the State Board exam a second time, the employee can no longer remain in the Nurse Graduate job. These employees can apply for any open jobs they qualify for, including jobs requiring a certification the employee currently holds (i.e., CNA, etc.). Failure to either pass boards or to be hired into another job will result in termination.

Registered Nurse graduates must be enrolled and have started coursework in the Intermountain Nurse Residency program before providing direct patient care (including direct patient care supervised by a licensed RN).

Posting Info:

  • Rate: Nursing Grad - $32.27, New Grad RN - $35.22
  • Shift: Monday through Friday, 8 hour shifts, no nights weekends, major holidays or call

Essential Functions

  • Demonstrates understanding of the steps in the nursing process and how the patient plan of care is developed, implemented, and revised to meet the needs of the patient (under direct supervision of an RN).
  • Assessment: Collects patient data (e.g., vital signs) under the direct supervision of the RN and reports significant changes in patient condition. Completes accurate documentation also under the direct supervision of the RN.
  • Planning: Observes and discusses with the RN the prioritization of patient needs among all patients assigned to their care during any one shift, and observes the development and modification of the interdisciplinary plan of care used to care for individual patients (under the direct supervision of the RN).

title: Controller - Real Estate & Construction - Atlanta, GA (Hybrid)
description:
Controller – Real Estate & Construction

Location: Roswell / Sandy Springs, GA
Work Environment: Initially in-office with potential for hybrid flexibility
Compensation: Competitive, based on experience

Position Overview

A rapidly growing, privately held real estate investment organization is seeking a hands-on Controller to lead accounting and financial reporting across a portfolio of related companies.

The organization operates multiple businesses focused on residential real estate acquisition, renovation and resale, rental properties, and real estate lending. As the business continues to grow, the company is bringing its accounting function in-house and needs an experienced accounting leader who can strengthen financial controls, improve reporting, and provide ownership with greater visibility into individual projects and overall business performance.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys an entrepreneurial, fast-moving environment and wants the opportunity to build and improve an accounting function rather than simply maintain established processes.

Key Responsibilities

  • Oversee accounting and financial reporting across approximately 6–8 related entities

  • Manage month-end close and produce accurate, timely financial statements

  • Establish and maintain accounting policies, procedures, and internal controls

  • Develop and maintain job costing by property and renovation project

  • Monitor renovation budgets, contractor costs, invoices, and project profitability

  • Identify cost overruns, billing discrepancies, and opportunities to strengthen financial controls

  • Provide ownership with timely reporting and visibility into individual properties and overall business performance

  • Manage accounting for residential property acquisitions, renovations, sales, and rental properties

  • Oversee accounting activities associated with real estate lending operations

  • Lead the transition of currently outsourced bookkeeping and accounting functions in-house

  • Manage intercompany activity and reporting across related entities

  • Oversee cash management, reconciliations, accounts payable, and general ledger activities

  • Partner with outside CPAs responsible for tax preparation and compliance

  • Coordinate with contractors and operational partners to ensure project costs are accurately captured and reported

  • Improve accounting systems, reporting processes, and financial controls as the organization grows

  • Assist ownership with additional financial, banking, insurance, and operational matters as needed

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field

  • Strong accounting experience within real estate, construction, homebuilding, property investment, or a closely related industry

  • Hands-on job costing or project accounting experience

  • Strong understanding of general ledger accounting, financial reporting, reconciliations, and month-end close

  • Experience working with multiple entities or related companies

  • Ability to develop and improve accounting processes and internal controls

  • Experience partnering with contractors, project managers, or operational teams

  • Strong working knowledge of QuickBooks, preferably QuickBooks Online

  • Comfortable working in an entrepreneurial environment where processes may need to be created or improved

  • Previous Controller, Assistant Controller, Accounting Manager, or similar experience preferred

Preferred Experience

  • CPA or CPA background is a plus but not required

  • Residential real estate acquisition, renovation, homebuilding, or real estate investment experience

  • Experience identifying project cost overruns and improving contractor or vendor controls

  • Experience bringing outsourced accounting or bookkeeping functions in-house

Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is a hands-on accounting professional who understands that effective accounting in a real estate and construction environment goes beyond producing financial statements.

This person can evaluate individual properties and renovation projects, understand where money is being spent, identify when costs are getting out of line, and establish practical controls that protect the business.

The successful candidate will be comfortable working directly with entrepreneurial ownership, contractors, outside CPAs, and other business partners. The environment is collaborative and informal, making this a strong fit for someone who is approachable, practical, flexible, and willing to roll up their sleeves.

Most importantly, this individual will help transform the accounting function from primarily historical reporting into a system that gives ownership timely financial information, stronger controls, and clear visibility into the profitability of each project and business.

Interested in learning more? Apply today for confidential consideration.
