title: Senior Project Manager/Associate Director, Discovery Project Management
description:
Who We Are:

Xenon Pharmaceuticals (NASDAQ:XENE) is a neuroscience-focused biopharmaceutical company dedicated to drug discovery, clinical development, and commercialization of life-changing therapeutics for patients in need. We are looking for great people who thrive in a respectful, collaborative, inclusive, and productive culture to join the Xenon team.

What We Do:

We are advancing an exciting product pipeline to address indications with high unmet medical need, including epilepsy, depression and pain. Our Phase 3 azetukalner program represents the most advanced, clinically validated potassium channel modulator in late-stage clinical development for multiple indications. In March 2026, we announced positive topline data from our Phase 3 X-TOLE2 study of azetukalner in focal onset seizures (FOS), and we anticipate submitting a New Drug Application to the Food and Drug Administration in the third quarter of 2026. Our Phase 3 epilepsy program also includes a second FOS study, X-TOLE3, which would support regulatory submissions outside the U.S., and the X-ACKT study in primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures, which would support regulatory submissions for an additional epilepsy indication. We also have multiple Phase 3 azetukalner clinical trials underway in major depressive disorder (MDD) and bipolar depression (BPD), based on topline data from our Phase 2 X-NOVA clinical trial. In addition, we are proud of our strong heritage in human genetics, deep understanding of ion channel biology, and expertise in novel chemistries to enable potent, selective ion channel targeting. We continue to advance an early-stage pipeline of novel therapeutic candidates, including Phase 1 studies for XEN1701 (targeting Nav1.7) and XEN1120 (targeting Kv7), which are important pain targets. Backed by a strong balance sheet to support our growth plans, we continue to build a fully integrated, premier neuroscience company with strong discovery, clinical development, corporate, and commercial operations.

About the Role:

We are seeking a Senior Project Manager/Associate Director, Discovery Project Management to join our team. This individual will work flexibly across a number of Discovery-stage small molecule programs. This role involves close coordination with stakeholders within Discovery (e.g., Chemistry, Biology, Compound Properties, Toxicology and CMC) and outside of Discovery (e.g., Finance, Legal, QA, Development).

This position reports to the Director, Discovery Project Management and will be based out of Vancouver, BC, Canada. The level of the position will be commensurate with the candidate’s education and industry experience. Hybrid positions require a minimum of two onsite days per week.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

· Develop and maintain comprehensive project/program/portfolio management and tracking tools addressing program scope, components, schedule and budget.

· Manage the Company’s Discovery-stage Contract Research Organizations (CROs) under both full-time equivalent and fee-for-service arrangements.

· Perform contract-related activities (drafting, contract change control, monitoring for performance, accepting deliverables, managing invoices and tracking accruals) relating to same within the scope of the Company’s contact management systems and policies.

· Coordinate Discovery-stage external studies including compound logistics, protocol drafting and review and communication with study directors.

· Coordinate project team, project sub-team, and functional group meetings for the Company’s Discovery stage programs. Track action items and timelines. Understand and communicate critical path towards key objectives. Schedule internal and external studies, as required.

· Facilitate cross-functional alignment with key Discovery stakeholders, identify potential cross-functional issues and bottlenecks across a multi-year horizon.

· Develop, optimize and manage data workflows and progression of compounds through program flowcharts. Ensure the timely distribution of externally-generated data and reports to appropriate stakeholders.

· Support activities that raise the scientific profile of the Company internally and externally, including Discovery training, Discovery invited speaker and Discovery events.

· Support Discovery scientific disclosure approvals under the Scientific Methods Based Disclosure Approval Process.

· Manage drafting, review and approval of Discovery preclinical reports to support regulatory filings.

· Develop and propose short- and long-term objectives for the function in accordance with overall Company strategies and plans.

· Act in accordance with Company policies, including, for example, the Code of Business Conduct and Ethics and ensure policies are understood and followed by direct reports, if any

· Other duties as assigned

QUALIFICATIONS:

· MSc or PhD in the fields of chemistry or biology

· At least 5 years' experience in drug discovery in the biotech or pharmaceutical industry

· Project management experience is preferred

· Excellent communication skills, both oral and written

· Highly organized with keen attention to detail

· Strong desire to manage projects to timeline and budget

· Ability to interface with internal and external stakeholders including scientists, executives, and members of the finance and legal departments; ability to influence colleagues in a cross-functional team environment

· Extensive intermediate to advanced computer skills (Power Point, Excel, Word, MS Project, SharePoint)

· Knowledge of project management methodology and technology, including developing Gantt Charts

· Willing and able to learn new skills to meet changing needs of the organization. Flexible and able to efficiently prioritize tasks

Our Total Rewards program includes base salary, target bonus, and stock options, as well as a full range of benefits including medical, dental, vision, short-& long-term disability, accidental death & dismemberment, and life insurance programs, Employee Assistance Program, travel insurance, and retirement savings programs with company matching contributions.

Xenon encourages time to rest and re-charge through vacation, personal days, sick days, and an end-of-year company shutdown. Xenon highly values employee development and has an expanding Training, Learning & Development program, including a Tuition Assistance program for advanced degrees.

description:
Role Overview
The Environmental, Health & Safety (EHS) Lead joins the Data Center Facility Operations
team to work closely with the global EHS team and local data center site management. This
on-site role is designed to develop and implement proven EHS programs, acting as a
thought leader to keep all data center employees and partners safe while working at the
facilities, ensuring strict compliance with EHS standards.


Responsibilities
The EHS Lead is responsible for delivering and tracking all necessary health and safety
training for onsite employees and contingent workers, maintaining accurate training
records. They identify and ensure compliance with all local, state, federal, and company
health, safety, and environmental policies, including tracking all necessary records and
documentation.


Providing functional direction to contracted services is a key duty, along with establishing
and growing positive cross-functional relationships with all site teams to gain alignment on
strategic priorities. The EHS Lead partners with vendors to uphold EHS requirements on
site and assists in the development and implementation of organization-wide EHS
standards and guidelines.


They develop site-based plans for the implementation and on-going management of global
EHS standards, building and maintaining a site safety posture that engages site leadership
and team members as active participants. The role involves managing activities to support
day-to-day EHS operations and partnering with relevant EHS professionals involved in
construction activities to ensure alignment. The EHS Lead actively supports incident
investigations, root cause analyses, and injury case management, maintains operational
safety programs, reviews site work procedures to assign risk levels, and participates in the
design of facilities and work procedures to make safety recommendations.

title: Software Engineer
description:
About Us

MintMCP helps companies put agents to work safely. We exist to help companies do more of their work with agents, and we build the infrastructure that makes a company's own work runnable by them. That has to start from trust. Our first product is an MCP gateway that gives those agents governed access to company data and tools.

Before agents can touch Slack, GitHub, Jira, Snowflake, internal databases, or production systems, you need to know what they can reach, what they did, and why they were allowed to do it. Most people carry far more permissions than any single task needs. If an agent uses your token directly, it inherits all of them. MintMCP scopes that access down to exactly what an agent needs to do its job and captures the data flows and audit logs security teams need. From there we are building the rest of the agent stack: connectors, monitoring, sandboxing, long-running agents, and memory, with the goal of becoming the system a company's work runs on.

We work in person in the San Francisco Bay Area. The structure is flat and the market moves fast, so you have a lot of latitude over what you work on and how.

AI-Native Startup

We are AI-native. Everyone uses Claude and Codex every day, and we have more agents than employees. They run in Slack alongside the team, write code, review PRs, and handle sales, marketing, and deal ops on the same gateway we sell to customers. We are building an entire company operating system around them, and you will help build it.

Traction

Since launching in February 2026, we have grown to 40+ paying customers, with strong inbound demand. Customers include Coursera, Arlo, and Braze. We are backed by Cowboy Ventures and Coatue, with angels including Frederic Kerrest (Okta), Michael Grinich (WorkOS), Andrej Karpathy, Jeff Dean, and Scott Belsky. Our founders are machine learning experts from Stanford, Berkeley, and CMU, with applied research at Google Brain and Waymo, and one co-founded Coursera.

The Job

You will own features end to end, from conception to production, across our gateway infrastructure, enterprise deployments, and agentic systems. The work leans backend and infra, but nothing is off limits: when the product needs a better UI you build it, and when a connector breaks during a security review you fix it.

Claude and Codex are your primary working environment, and you use a fleet of agents to move faster than a team this size has any right to. Agents write much of the code and review PRs, so your real job is the judgment they cannot make: shaping the problem, making architecture, product, and UX calls, hardening enterprise paths, designing connectors, protecting security-sensitive surfaces, and catching generated code that is quietly wrong. Roles are blurred and we ship within hours, and you will learn directly from the founders and from customers.

We hire across levels, from strong early-career builders to seasoned engineers, and we set level and pay to match. What matters most is judgment, range, and how fast you ship.

About You

  • You are a builder with a track record of shipping to real users, whether that is a product, an internal tool, an open-source project, or a serious side project. You ship, then iterate, without waiting for specs or approvals.

  • You have strong fundamentals and learn fast. How quickly you pick things up matters as much as years of experience.

  • You care about product value and customer needs over technical purity.

  • You take infra seriously. You think about blast radius, trust boundaries, and what happens when your code is in the path of every customer's agents.

  • You can read unfamiliar code, reason from first principles, and explain your tradeoffs.

  • You are comfortable across the stack (TypeScript, Python, CockroachDB), or you pick up new languages, protocols, and domains fast.

  • You are excited to build with agents, and to learn when they help and when they hide a problem.

  • You already build with AI every day and want room to move without heavy process.

Nice to have:

  • Developer-facing products, protocol or gateway work, or infrastructure at scale.

  • Background in security, identity, or permission systems.

  • Contributions to open source, MCP servers, or agentic frameworks.

  • Design sensibility: engineers who care about design, designers who think about infrastructure.

What we offer:

  • Competitive compensation and meaningful equity.

  • Unusual scope and ownership of features that ship to enterprise customers.

  • Building and deploying agents on the same platform we sell.

  • Direct access to the founders, customer context, and product direction, with mentorship as you grow.

  • Health benefits, on a team that puts family and health first.

title: Director of Data
description:
About Patlytics:

Patlytics is the fastest-growing AI-native patent intelligence platform, transforming how IP is protected and monetized at scale. Our advanced LLMs and generative AI engine—custom-built for intellectual property—power every phase of the patent workflow from invention disclosure through litigation, delivering citation-backed insights with unprecedented accuracy and speed.

Fresh off our $40M Series B — led by SignalFire, with participation from N47, Myriad Venture Partners, Liquid 2 Ventures, BAM Corner Point, Alumni Ventures, Antiportfolio Ventures and Relativity- allows us to triple down on the product, accelerate growth globally, hire future mission-aligned colleagues, and to continue redefining what is possible for our customers. — we're scaling fast across product, engineering, and go-to-market. If you want to build at the inflection point, this is it.

With teams across the globe we're building a global company fueled by exceptional talent and bold ideas. Our rapid expansion is driven by people who bring entrepreneurial energy, intellectual curiosity, and a shared commitment to setting the global standard for AI-powered IP intelligence. We're creating a culture where diverse perspectives shape breakthrough innovation and every voice contributes to transforming how the world protects ideas.

We hire for trajectory, not just credentials. If you're 70% of this list and hungry to close the gap, apply.

The Role:

Reporting to the VP of Finance & Operations, the Director of Data will own the end-to-end data stack across GTM (Sales, Customer Success, Strategy), Marketing, Finance, and Product. You will partner closely with the executive team to build centralized sources of truth for the company's most important metrics and stand up the data infrastructure that helps Patlytics scale past $50-100M+ in ARR. You are not afraid to roll up your sleeves as an individual contributor while designing and building the data function from the ground up. A trusted partner within the business and to the executive team, you will turn fragmented data across systems into the single, reliable foundation on which the company plans, reports, and operates. This is an exciting and rare opportunity to embark on a journey with a fast-growing company and deliver on highly impactful work - even better if you've seen this growth play out before and want to join at an earlier stage.

What You'll Accomplish:

  • Data Infrastructure & Engineering: Design, build, and own the modern data stack end-to-end - ingestion, warehousing, transformation, orchestration, and analysis/BI. You'll architect scalable pipelines that connect source systems across GTM, Marketing, Finance, and Product into a governed, centralized warehouse built to support the company well past $50-100M+ ARR.

  • Single Source of Truth: Define, document, and maintain the canonical metrics that run the business - ARR, pipeline, retention, usage, unit economics - so that Sales, Customer Success, Finance, Marketing, and Product are all operating off the same numbers. You'll build the metrics dictionary, own data quality and reconciliation, and eliminate the version-control chaos of competing spreadsheets and siloed datasets.

  • Analytics & Visualization: Deliver the reporting and dashboard layer that gives the executive team, board, and department leaders real-time visibility into performance. You'll pair strong data analysis with clear visualization to surface the "aha" insights that influence big business decisions.

  • Tools & Automation: You have an eye for technology and efficiency and will help Patlytics build out its data infrastructure for scale - increasing automation, reducing manual reporting, and lowering the risk of errors. You'll evaluate and select vendors, oversee implementations and integrations, and enhance checks and controls across the stack.

  • Business Partnering / Cross-Functional Collaboration: Serve as the data partner to the executive team and department leaders - translating business questions into data models, instrumenting new initiatives, and supporting planning, forecasting, and board reporting with trusted data.

  • Ad-Hoc Projects: Assist in the planning and execution of key operational projects such as performance dashboards, custom reporting by dimension for different departments, GTM funnel instrumentation, pricing and usage analyses, and diligence-ready data packages.

Who You Are:

Experience:

  • 7+ years of experience in data engineering, data infrastructure, analytics engineering, or equivalent. Additionally, you have high-growth SaaS / Technology company experience in the range of $30-150M+ in ARR - you've seen what breaks at scale and know how to build ahead of it.

  • Strong competency in data infrastructure and data engineering, with complementary skills in data analysis and governance - you can build the pipes and tell the story of what flows through them.

  • Strong fluency and familiarity with Snowflake, Databricks, Clickhouse, Hubspot, Salesforce, Quickbooks, Fivetran, dbt, Netsuite, and mySQL - you will identify where automation can be leveraged, help select vendors, and oversee implementation as applicable.

  • Experience partnering across GTM, Marketing, Finance, and Product, with a working understanding of AI and SaaS business models and the metrics that matter to each function.

You have:

  • A design / infrastructure mindset - you look at how data models, pipelines, and reports are built, think about how they can be architected better and what data feeds them, and how to connect tools and information harmoniously.

  • A 'do-er' mentality with high motor and energy - you are a highly resourceful self-starter who takes charge, rolls your sleeves up, and gets the job done as an individual contributor while building for scale.

  • An obsession with data accuracy and meticulous attention to detail - you take pride in every number being right, reconciled, and trusted across the company.

  • A strong ability to develop, document, and build frameworks to enable scalability of a fast-growing company.

  • A passion for data-driven discussions and giving the business a narrative - you find ways to bring deep insights that influence big business decisions, and executives trust your recommendations.

  • An excitement to work in a fast-moving and growing company - you are highly adaptable and understand startup environments.

  • An ability to communicate crisply across altitudes - equally comfortable presenting metrics to the board and debating schema design with engineers

This role is NOT for you if:

  • You're looking for a 9-5.

  • You're unable to build processes and infrastructure in chaotic, hypergrowth environments where “the plane is being built in flight” - ambiguity and speed are features of this role, not bugs.

description:

  • Provide initial fault isolation and propose resolutions for approval by senior colleagues to address network or server issues promptly and limit business disruption.

  • Use the knowledge management system to access specific technical information and contribute to the internal knowledge base for the benefit of the IT team.

  • Contribute to reviewing existing tasks in own area of work, collecting ideas for infrastructure improvement and closing existing skills gaps within the networking domain.

Skills:

Required:

  • Problem Resolution: Monitors, diagnoses, and fixes problems with technology products, specifically focusing on server health and network connectivity.

  • Technical Troubleshooting: Identifies and resolves technical problems in line with prescribed solution options and industry standards.

  • Systems Testing: Designs, executes, and reports on systems/service tests to ensure applications and hardware function as specified in requirements.

  • Implementation Planning: Reviews and evaluates recommendations to develop appropriate plans for software/hardware rollouts.

  • Infrastructure Management: Installs, sets up, configures, and manages software, environments, and On-Prem VOIP systems.

  • OS Administration: Expertly sets up and maintains operating systems (Windows/Linux) and server environments.

  • Security & Compliance: Maintains systems/services and information security, integrity, and continuity.

  • Networking Proficiency: Deep understanding of TCP/IP networking; able to troubleshoot and manage complex network configurations.

  • Data Analysis: Determines and analyzes trends from collected system data to assist in compiling reports for leadership decision-making.

  • Cloud & Virtualization: Proficiently navigates and manages cloud-based infrastructure, including virtual machines, networks, and storage.

  • Adaptability: Shifts mental mindsets to assess the facts of a current situation (e.g., a critical outage) and makes innovative adjustments to thinking to thrive in any scenario.

Education and Experience:

  • Education: Bachelor's Degree or Equivalent Level.

  • Experience: Experienced practitioner able to work unsupervised with a focus on servers and networking (1 to 3 years).

  • Managerial Experience: Very limited coordination of others or help-desk oversight (0 to 3 months).

As a trailblazer in the cannabis industry, we’re committed to providing a holistic approach to well-being, fostering a community where every patient and customer can thrive and find relief.

Who We Are:

iAnthus Capital Management is a multi-state operator, encompassing the full spectrum of cannabis enterprises, from cultivation to processing to retailing. Cannabis will be the next great transformative industry - not just because it has the power to change people’s lives (especially those suffering from chronic ailments) – but also because it will impact many other industries, from agriculture to pharmaceuticals to alcoholic beverages. Our mission is to create the most valuable cannabis brands and network of cannabis operations and distribution nationally. At iAnthus, you will be given opportunities for career development, a flexible work environment, excellent benefits, a wellness program and the ability to interact with and learn from leaders in the cannabis industry.

Who You Are:

You have a strong desire to learn and to contribute to a team. You are passionate about making an inclusive, positive, and compliant workforce. You can effectively manage your time and focus on ensuring data integrity and accuracy for your projects. If you would like to work in a fast-paced environment and are interested in building something meaningful with the rest of the iAnthus team, we would love to hear from you!


Benefits:

Summary:

As a Dispensary Associate, you’ll be a vital force in the evolving world of cannabis. Acting as a trusted advisor, you’ll be at the forefront of patient acquisition for medicinal cannabis and welcoming adult-use use customers, fostering an environment where education, exploration, and satisfaction intersect. Your primary responsibility is to offer comprehensive education on strains, effects, and various methods of cannabis use, ensuring everyone receives tailored information to make informed decisions. Beyond education, you’ll be the face of our dispensary, delivering warm and informed service, recording transactions in the POS system, and collaborating closely with dispensary managers to maintain a clean and organized dispensary environment.

Essential Functions:

The Dispensary Associate elevates the dispensary experience for our patients and customers. This role is the heartbeat of our interactions, where you’ll be a vital part of shaping a positive, informative, and seamless journey for prospective, new, and returning customers. Your key responsibilities include, but is not limited to the following:

  • Welcome everyone with a friendly attitude, creating a positive dispensary experience.

  • Proactively interact with customers, guide them through our product offerings, and highlight exclusive specials to increase sales opportunities.
  • Enter and access patient records accurately, confirming identities and eligibility to purchase in line with legal and company standards.
  • Represent the company’s brand well as a brand ambassador.
  • Follows and uphold the company’s core values, including respect, diversity, sustainability, research, and service.
  • Adheres to iAnthus' cultural principles of collaboration, innovation, and accountability.
  • Accurately handle transactions, receiving payments with a smile, and recording purchases in our Dispensary Management System.
  • Provide patients and customers with informative printed materials, helping them make well-informed decisions.
  • Bring a sales-focused attitude to every shift, always looking for chances to increase sales and grow business.
  • Work with Dispensary Managers to check product inventory, making sure we have a diverse and fresh selection that meets our patients' and customers’ needs.
  • Maintain a clean and organized dispensary area.
  • Additional duties and responsibilities as assigned.

This job description is not intended to cover or contain a comprehensive list of activities. This description reflects managements’ assignment of essential functions, and it does not restrict the tasks that may be assigned. Duties and responsibilities may change at any time with or without notice.

Your willingness to contribute to the evolving needs of our team is highly valued.


Qualifications + Education:

  • Must be twenty-one (21) years of age or older
  • High School diploma or equivalent is required.
  • Must have a valid driver's license and reliable transportation.
  • Exceptional interpersonal skills with a passion for delivering top-notch customer service.
  • Ability to work independently, coordinate multiple tasks, and prioritize work effectively.
  • Reliability is a must.
  • Meticulous organizational skills with acute attention to detail.
  • Computer-savvy, with a knack for quickly mastering new software.
  • Knowledge of or willingness to learn state-specific cannabis laws and regulatory compliance is non-negotiable.
  • Comfortable teaching customers about the medicinal and adult-use aspects of cannabis and conducting workshops or info sessions to boost their understanding and confidence in choosing products.
  • Ganjier certification preferred

Starting Pay Rate: $15/hr


Working Conditions:

The employee works in a medical dispensary environment and uses a computer, telephone, and other office equipment to perform duties. This is a hands-on, customer-facing position. The position will regularly interact with the public and needs to engage patients and customers in a friendly and helpful manner. The employee must be able to function effectively in a high-paced, fast-moving retail environment. The employee may be subjected to work in environments that include exposure to, but not limited to, fumes, dust, odors, heights, indoor A/C, no A/C, motion and noise.

The position also requires a high level of scheduling flexibility and will occasionally include evening, weekend, and holiday work hours. The employee will encounter frequent interruptions throughout the workday and must have a high regard for self-management, time management, and scheduling of activities.


Physical Requirements:

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to remain in a stationary position 80% of the time, move around, and clearly communicate. The employee must constantly position oneself to move freely around the store. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 50 pounds with assistance. The employee will often need to use a ladder, with up to a 12’ extension and general hardware tools.

Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus.

title: Design Verification Engineer (Lab Project Specialist)
description:
Position Summary

We are seeking an experienced Lab Project Specialist to lead the planning, development, and execution of verification activities for medical device products. This individual will serve as a technical expert in device testing, design inputs, risk analyses, and product requirements into robust verification strategies and test methods.

The ideal candidate possesses a strong engineering background, understands how medical devices function from both a design and user perspective, and can independently determine what testing is required to demonstrate that design requirements have been met. This role works closely with R&D, Lab, Quality, Regulatory Affairs, and external partners throughout the product development lifecycle.

Key Responsibilities

Design Verification

  • Develop and execute design verification strategies for new and existing medical devices.
  • Review product requirements, design inputs, and risk analyses to determine appropriate verification activities.
  • Create verification protocols, test plans, acceptance criteria, and reports in compliance with applicable design control requirements.
  • Ensure objective evidence is generated to demonstrate compliance with design requirements.

Test Method Development and Test Execution

  • Identify and implement appropriate measurement systems, instrumentation, fixtures, and data acquisition methods.
  • Evaluate test method capability, repeatability, and reproducibility (e.g., GR&R).
  • Develop custom test equipment and fixtures as needed.
  • Support TMV and testing execution.

Data Analysis and Technical Reporting

  • Analyze test data using statistical and engineering methods.
  • Support root cause analysis and recommend corrective actions.
  • Prepare clear technical reports and present findings to project teams and management.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Collaborate with Design Engineering, Quality, Regulatory Affairs, and Lab staff.
  • Coordinate testing activities with external laboratories, consultants, and suppliers.
  • Mentor junior engineers and provide leadership in verification and testing practices.
  • Support overall project planning from a testing strategy perspective.

Compliance and Quality

  • Ensure verification activities comply with applicable standards, guidance documents, and internal procedures.
  • Participate in Design Control, Risk Management, and Design History File (DHF) activities.
  • Expertise in ISO 13485, ISO 14971

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Systems Engineering, or related discipline.
  • 3+ years of experience in medical device development, verification, testing, or systems engineering.
  • Demonstrated experience developing verification strategies and executing design verification programs.
  • Strong understanding of medical device design controls and product development processes.
  • Experience developing test methods and analyzing data.
  • Excellent technical writing and communication skills.
  • Ability to independently assess designs and determine appropriate verification approaches.
  • Ability to work in a lab and/or clean room environment requiring PPE

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with inhalation, drug delivery, combination products, surgical, diagnostic, or other complex medical devices.
  • Knowledge of risk management and failure analysis methodologies.
  • Experience with statistical analysis tools such as Minitab, JMP, or equivalent.
  • Familiarity with IEC 60601, ISO 11608, or other applicable medical device standards.
  • Experience managing external test laboratories and contract development partners.

At Nemera, we prioritize patients when creating drug delivery devices, understanding that accurate dosing and ergonomics are crucial for treatment adherence. title: SCALES Director of Operations
description:
The Director of Operations provides strategic leadership and operational oversight for Vanderbilt Center for Simulation, Computational-modeling, and AI-integrated Learning for Engineering Systems (SCALES). Reporting to the Center Director, this position is responsible for managing the Center's research administration, financial operations, educational initiatives, communications, strategic partnerships, and day-to-day operations. The Director serves as the primary operational liaison among faculty, university administrative offices, funding agencies, industry partners, and external stakeholders, ensuring the successful execution of SCALES' mission while supporting the Center's growth and national prominence.


Key Functions and Expected Performance:
Leadership & Personnel Management
- Oversee the Center's administrative and operational staff, providing strategic leadership and ensuring the effective execution of the Center's mission and priorities.
- Recruit, hire, onboard, train, supervise, mentor, and evaluate professional and support staff in accordance with university policies and best practices.
- Manage a small- to mid-sized team of experienced professionals, typically at junior and intermediate levels, providing leadership, direction, coaching, and performance management while fostering professional growth and accountability.
- Lead, direct, and review the work of staff who exercise independent judgment and latitude in carrying out assignments, ensuring consistency, quality, and alignment with Center objectives.
- Establish performance expectations, delegate responsibilities, prioritize workloads, and implement operational policies and strategies that support organizational effectiveness and continuous improvement.

- Foster a collaborative, inclusive, and service-oriented workplace culture that reflects Vanderbilt University's values of excellence, integrity, innovation, respect, and teamwork.
- Promote effective communication, collaboration, and cross-functional partnerships among Center staff, faculty, university administrative offices, and external stakeholders.
- Identify staffing needs and organizational opportunities to support the Center's continued growth and evolving strategic priorities.
- Develop and implement administrative policies, standard operating procedures, and best practices to enhance operational efficiency, service delivery, and organizational effectiveness
- Oversee the day to day operations of SCALES


Financial Management
- Oversee the financial operations of the Center, including operating budgets, discretionary funds, sponsored project accounts, and strategic investments.
- Establish, implement, and manage transparent and comprehensive budget plans to monitor expenditures, revenue, cost allocations, and fund utilization across all Center programs and initiatives.
- Collaborate with Vanderbilt Finance and university administrative offices to develop annual budgets, financial forecasts, and long-range operational plans that support the Center's strategic goals.
- Prepare financial reports, analyze budget performance, and provide recommendations to support informed decision-making by Center leadership.
- Ensure responsible financial stewardship through effective fiscal planning, resource allocation, and monitoring of financial performance.
- Ensure compliance with university financial policies, sponsor requirements, and applicable regulations while promoting the efficient and effective use of Center resources.
- Identify opportunities to optimize operational efficiencies and strategically allocate resources to support the Center's research, educational, and outreach priorities.


Research Administration
- Serve as the primary operational resource for SCALES faculty throughout the proposal development and award lifecycle.
- Coordinate with Vanderbilt Contracts & Grants, Sponsored Programs Administration, and other university offices to facilitate proposal submissions and award management.
- Assist faculty with proposal documentation, budgets, compliance requirements, and resolution of time-sensitive proposal issues.
- Support post-award administrative coordination for sponsored research projects.
- Monitor the SCALES general email account and respond to requests from faculty, industry, government agencies, and external collaborators.
- Develop and maintain relationships with industry partners interested in SBIR/STTR collaborations.
- Maintain and communicate a database of industry partners and funding collaboration opportunities available to SCALES faculty.

Communications & External Engagement
- Lead development and implementation of the Center's communications strategy.
- Coordinate the design, launch, and ongoing management of the SCALES website through university resources or external vendors.
- Promote the Center's visibility through strategic communications and external outreach.
- Represent the center operationally in relevant university committees and working groups


Center Operations, Events & Strategic Initiatives
- Oversee the planning, coordination, and execution of high-profile conferences, workshops, symposia, seminar series, and strategic initiatives, ensuring alignment with the Center's mission and Vanderbilt University's brand standards.
- Coordinate the SCALES Seminar Series, including speaker invitations, scheduling, logistics, communications, and event execution.
- Manage visits for scholars, faculty, researchers, students, industry representatives, and international collaborators.
- In collaboration of CEE staff, coordinate conferences and workshops where SCALES serves as the primary organizer or co-organizer, including national and international meetings.
- Ensure successful execution of multiple concurrent events while maintaining exceptional operational quality and stakeholder engagement.


Advisory Board & External Relations
- Coordinate the activities of the SCALES External Advisory Board.
- Organize annual Advisory Board meetings, prepare agendas, meeting materials, and follow-up communications.
- Serve as the primary liaison with Advisory Board members, funding agencies, industry partners, and external collaborators.


Supervisory Relationships:
This position does have supervisory responsibility, this position reports administratively and functionally to the Director of SCALES

Education and Certifications
- Bachelor’s Degree is necessary
- Masters is preferred


Experience and Skills:
- Minimum of 5 years of experience in operations, administrative management, financial management, grant/contract administration or related roles—preferably in research, academic or interdisciplinary setting.
- Understands basic management approaches such as work scheduling, prioritizing,
coaching and process execution.
- University/College background – Engineering preferred
- Strong Organizational skills
- Strong critical thinking/ problem solving skills
- Experience working with senior leadership
- Experience working in a higher education/ academic setting preferred
- Financial background including the review of budgets
- Proficient in Microsoft office, adobe, and have database experience
- Comfort with new technological systems. Adapts easily to changes in technology and process
- Ability to work on multiple projects simultaneously
- Professional and pleasant attitude with considerable tact, diplomacy, and judgment in interactions with students, faculty, and staff

title: Data Center Facilities Technician, Electrical
description:
The Data Center team designs and operates some of the most sophisticated electrical engineering, mechanical engineering and HVAC systems in the world. Facilities Technicians at Google data centers operate, monitor and support physical facilities conditions. Some of these duties will include heating and cooling of air and water, power supply, generators, UPS systems, electrical distribution and control and monitoring systems. You regularly help inspect, maintain and repair various data center systems such as piping and non-critical electrical or mechanical system components). You provide daily assistance to senior technicians as you read blueprints/schematics, conduct tours of systems and assess their working order.

As an advocate for best practices, you develop creative approaches to reducing operational costs while improving overall data center efficiency. You ensure that environmental and safety standards are consistently met, identifying problems and making repairs quickly. In emergency situations or abnormal conditions, you manage data center performance issues and outages to minimize the recovery time from failures.

As a Facilities Technician, you will operate, monitor, and support physical facilities conditions for our data centers.

The AI and Infrastructure team is redefining what’s possible. We empower Google customers with breakthrough capabilities and insights by delivering AI and Infrastructure at unparalleled scale, efficiency, reliability and velocity. Our customers include Googlers, Google Cloud customers, and billions of Google users worldwide.

We're the driving team behind Google's groundbreaking innovations, empowering the development of our cutting-edge AI models, delivering unparalleled computing power to global services, and providing the essential platforms that enable developers to build the future. From software to hardware our teams are shaping the future of world-leading hyperscale computing, with key teams working on the development of our TPUs, Vertex AI for Google Cloud, Google Global Networking, Data Center operations, systems research, and much more.

Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

US: $86000 - $118000 (USD) + 15% bonus target + equity + benefits

Learn more about benefits at Google.
  • Inspect, maintain, and repair various data center systems.
  • Provide daily assistance to technicians as you read blueprints/schematics/sequence of operations, conduct tours of systems, and assess their working order.
  • Manage the uptime and maintenance of UPS, generators, electrical distribution, and control and monitoring systems.
  • Operate, monitor, maintain, and respond to abnormal conditions in the data center facilities systems and equipment.
  • Support startup, commissioning, and integration of new electrical equipment and systems into facilities infrastructure.

Minimum qualifications:

  • Associate's degree, trade school certification, or other certified training in a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 2 years of electrical experience (e.g., electrical testing equipment or electrical distribution) in an industrial or commercial environment.

  • Experience in data centers, hospitals, or power plants.

4. Demonstrated interpersonal skills that convey a positive and supportive attitude.

title: Assistant Director of Finance
description:
Pay Range: $75,000-$90,000

Position Summary

As a member of the professional staff, contributes specialized knowledge and skill in a discipline (e.g. Accounting, Finance, Human Resources, Information Resources, Operations Planning & Support, Sales & Marketing) area to support team and/or department business objectives. Generally works under limited supervision, but within established guidelines, producing and analyzing more complex business information to assist in the decision-making process.

Finance & Accounting – Context of Role

The Resort Operations Finance team at MVW is on a multi-year journey to build a team designed for impact, not transactions. We've made our roles outcome-based: you'll own decisions and create value as a trusted finance business partner embedded with site resort leaders and Boards members driving revenue, adjusted EBITDA, and cost management outcomes. With transactional work, e.g. AP, AR, month-end, reconciliations, audits, and billing, handled by our external managed service provider, you'll focus on delivering insights, ensuring governance, and achieving results. Success is measured by impacts across multiple properties giving you broad exposure and meaningful participation.

Job Summary

The Assistant Director of Finance (Assistant DOF) – Resort Operations is an emerging, field-based finance leader who serves in a supporting role to a Market Director of Finance (MDOF) within a market of up to 12 resorts.

The Assistant DOF performs resort operations finance responsibilities, e.g., financial business partnership to resort leaders, financial guidance and support to property owner association board members, and financial oversight for up to five small associations within a market allowing a MDOF to focus on larger, more complex properties. Operating in a model where core accounting and transactional activities are delivered through Shared Services via a Managed Service Provider (MSP), the ADOF translates financial information into actionable insights and assists in identifying and executing revenue and savings opportunities.

The ADOF helps ensure compliance with Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP), Sarbanes-Oxley, MVW policies, and association governing documents, while building professional capabilities expected of a future field-based Director of Finance role.

Working Relationships

  • Market Director of Finance (MDOF)

  • Corporate Resort Operations Finance Teams

  • Regional and Site Resort Operations Leaders

  • Property Owner Association Board Members

  • Managed Service Provider (MSP) / Shared Services

  • Legal and Corporate Partners

  • Third-Party Stakeholders

Expected Contributions

  • Performs more complex quantitative and qualitative analysis for business processes and/or projects. Often manages small projects, business processes or parts of larger ones.

  • Responds to, solves and makes decisions on more complex/non-routine business requests with limited to moderate risk.

  • Responsible for own work and contributing to team, department and/or business results. May direct work of non-management staff.

  • Assists more senior associates in achieving business results by:

    • identifying opportunities to enhance the effectiveness of business processes.

    • providing training and technical guidance to less senior staff, where appropriate, and serving as point-of-contact for problem resolution.

    • participating in setting department operating plans.

    • recognizing and celebrating team successes.

    • achieving results against budget within scope of responsibility.

  • Demonstrates an awareness of personal strengths and areas for improvement and acts independently to improve and increase skills and knowledge.

  • Performs other duties as appropriate.

Expected Contributions

Business Partnership & Financial Support

  • Serves as an assistant finance business partner to Resort Operations leaders at assigned properties, providing fact-based insights and clear trade-offs to support decision-making.

  • Develops annual business plans, budgets, and rolling forecasts for assigned associations and ancillary operations.

  • Translates financial results and market analytics into decision-grade insights, including variance analysis, trends, and recommended actions.

  • Builds trusted relationships with on-site leaders, corporate partners, and third-party stakeholders to enable timely, informed decisions.

Property Owner Association & Board Governance Support

  • Supports handling board governance and financial matters for 3–5 of the smaller associations within a market, mirroring the MDOF's responsibilities on a smaller scale.

  • Reviews board materials prepared by MSP, e.g., financial statements, budgets, forecasts, and reserve funding for accuracy and completeness.

  • Presents fee and capital-priority trade-offs and manage board communications on financial matters.

  • Proactively identifies, elevates and resolves board and association issues, partnering with Legal and corporate teams as needed.

  • Ensures adherence to management agreements and association governing documents across assigned nonprofit property owners' associations.

  • Coordinates reserve planning and required board approvals, supporting compliant financial packages for each jurisdiction.

Revenue & Savings Opportunity Execution

  • Supports identifying, implementing, and executing revenue growth and cost-savings opportunities including ancillary revenue, Cost of Goods Sold (COGS), labor productivity, and controllable expenses.

  • Translates market playbooks and benchmarking insights into site-level action plans and supports operating leaders through execution.

  • Tracks initiatives against baselines, quantify realized value, and surface replicable best practices.

  • Supports maintenance fee mitigation and EBITDA improvement efforts that protect owner value and guest experiences.

Reporting, Controls & MSP Oversight

  • Oversees MSP outputs for assigned associations, e.g., confirming accuracy, timeliness, and adherence to defined requirements – without performing transactional processing.

  • Reviews key financial deliverables, e.g., monthly/quarterly/annual financial statements, critical journal entries, and reconciliations, and ensures exceptions are investigated and resolved.

  • Ensures compliance with GAAP, Sarbanes-Oxley, MVW policies, and association governing documents, escalating issues proactively.

  • Supports internal, external, tax, and regulatory audit readiness and drives continuous improvement in processes, controls, and reporting transparency.

Regional Support

  • Supports an MDOF within a market, e.g., providing coverage for larger properties, completing special projects, and managing small project market-wide initiatives.

  • Prepares and delivers ad hoc analyses, forecasting support, and decision-support materials that strengthen the market's strategic finance agenda.

  • Builds readiness for future career growth by developing leadership, business-partnering, and governance capabilities.

  • Performs other reasonable job duties as requested.

Candidate Profile

Successful candidates should possess knowledge and experience and demonstrate strong leadership and relationship skills as follows:

  • Generally, a professional position with specific knowledge in a discipline (e.g., Accounting, Human Resources, Information Resources).

  • College degree and/or relevant experience typically required.

Candidate Profile

Education

  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, or in a related discipline or equivalent work experience.

Certifications Preferred

  • Certified Management Accountant (CMA)

  • Hospitality Finance (CHAE)

  • FP&A Certifications (FPAC/FMVA)

  • Community-association (CMCA/AMS/PCAM) credentials are a plus.

Experience

  • At least five years of progressive experience in finance and accounting roles that support field-based business operations.

  • Experience as a finance business partner or stakeholder management preferred.

  • Experience in Hotel Management, Vacation Ownership, Hospitality preferred.

  • Experience coordinating and working with multiple resources, both internal resources and external vendors, to accomplish tasks preferred.

Skills and Attributes

Financial & Analytical

  • Ability to plan, analyze, and forecast – skilled in developing business plans, budgets, and rolling forecasts and in translating financial results and market analytics into decision-grade insights, including variance analysis, trend identification, and recommended actions.

  • Ability to drive revenue and savings outcomes – skilled in identifying and executing revenue and cost-savings opportunities, e.g., ancillary revenue, COGS, labor productivity, controllable expenses, etc., converting benchmarking insights into site-level action plans, and tracking initiatives to quantify realized value.

Governance, Controls & Oversight

  • Ability to ensure compliance and maintain controls – skilled in applying GAAP, Sarbanes-Oxley, MVW policies, and association governing documents; reviewing key deliverables and reconciliations; and proactively escalating exceptions and risks.

  • Ability to support board and association governance – skilled in supporting board governance for assigned associations, presenting fee and capital-priority trade-offs, managing financial communications, and coordinating reserve planning and required approvals.

  • Ability to oversee vendor and service delivery – Skilled in overseeing Managed Service Provider outputs for accuracy, timeliness, and adherence to requirements, and in managing the relationship without performing transactional processing.

Partnership, Relationships & Influence

  • Ability to partner as a trusted finance advisor – skilled in serving as a finance business partner to resort operations leaders, providing fact-based insights and clear trade-offs that inform and influence operational decisions.

  • Ability to build relationships and manage stakeholders – skilled in establishing trusted relationships with on-site leaders, corporate partners, third-party stakeholders, and board members to enable timely, informed decisions across the market.

  • Ability to communicate and influence – skilled in conveying complex financial information clearly and persuasively to both financial and non-financial audiences to drive action and alignment.

title: Term-Senior Data Analyst- Prenatal-to-3 Policy Impact center
description:
Job Description Summary:

The Prenatal-to-3 Policy Impact Center aims to accelerate states’ implementation of evidence- based policies that help all children thrive from the start.

We seek an experienced Senior Research Data Analyst to provide data management and analysis expertise to projects across the Center. The role primarily includes original survey and program data cleaning, data management, and statistical analyses for a portfolio of original research and evaluation projects. The Policy Impact Center’s research seeks to build the evidence base in key areas related to the impact of state policies and programs on outcomes for infants, toddlers, and their families. The role of the Senior Research Data Analyst is essential for transforming raw data into research assets, ensuring the validity and credibility of the Center’s research, resolving complex data challenges, and supporting timely research-based deliverables.

This Senior Research Data Analyst position provides essential data expertise and rigorous analytic support and guidance to a team of data researchers responsible for supporting the Center’s goals to build the evidence base for effective and equitable policymaking, track state progress in building a more effective and equitable system of care, and shape policy development in states through targeted assistance and support.

General Notes:

This position is a term appointment for 12 months beginning upon date of hire, and reports functionally and administratively to the Director of Data and Analytics, Kels Bowman. Applicants from underrepresented groups are encouraged to apply. We are committed to building an inclusive and diverse environment to continue to build a strong and equitable prenatal-to-3 system of care. This position can be performed remotely, and hybrid remote-work opportunities are available. Visa sponsorship is unavailable for this position.

The primary responsibilities of the position include data management, analysis, and writing

  • Contribute to the development of research questions, study designs, analytic plans, and methodological approaches for original research and evaluation projects

  • Manage survey data cleaning and preparation, including guiding processes for data collection and testing, providing support in developing the analytic plan and analysis timeline, implementing quality assurance protocols and detailed documentation, constructing clean, validated analytic datasets that serve as the foundation for the Center’s portfolio of original research

  • Contribute to the development, programming, testing, and refinement of surveys, including reviewing measures, response options, skip logic, and data structures to ensure alignment with research questions and analytic plans

  • Work independently with messy, real-world data and exercise judgment in resolving data quality issues, missing data, and documentation challenges, ensuring analytic datasets are defensible

  • Acquire, manage, and analyze raw datasets, including administrative data from state agencies and national longitudinal sources such as Census, with demonstrated ability to merge datasets, clean and prepare data for analysis, and assess representativeness, processes essential to the Center’s research goals

  • Interpret data and independently select and apply appropriate statistical tests, analyze results, and provide ongoing reports

  • Contribute to and/or lead the production of written products and academic publications translating the results of policy research and analyses into actionable insights for stakeholders and state policymakers.

Project Management and Leadership:

  • Ensure the methodological quality, validity, and integrity of all research analyses conducted, considering the most rigorous possible analytic approaches, appropriate assumptions and interpretation, and careful documentation

  • Communicate effectively with key project staff to ensure they are appropriately informed of project progress, key decisions, and emerging issues

  • Take a leadership role in managing data processes including data collection, management, and analysis

  • Monitor compliance with data security and data retention policies to maintain and ensure

the integrity of the Center’s data and research

  • Coordinate with clients and stakeholders, as necessary to obtain and manage administrative datasets

  • Contribute to developing and improving processes and procedures

  • Mentor and train staff in survey data cleaning, analytic workflows, and team processes

  • Monitor and supervise students to effectively contribute to projects

Supervisory Relationships:

This position may supervise students and does not have staff supervisory responsibility.

Required/Essential Qualifications:

  • Exceptional interpersonal skills and an ability to work collaboratively with others in a team environment

  • Experience conducting data management, cleaning, and analysis using original survey data

  • Strong skills in R

  • Exceptional analytic and critical thinking skills

  • Excellent project management and organizational skills, strong problem-solving abilities, tenacity about details and organization

  • Strong written communication skills, including the ability to synthesize complex concepts clearly and concisely

  • Experience contributing to original research or program evaluation projects, including developing analytic plans, documenting methods, and interpreting findings

  • Ability to come up to speed on new topics quickly, multi-task effectively, and produce high-quality work under time constraints; flexible and able to adapt to changing timelines and circumstances when needed

  • Demonstrated understanding and support for key concepts in diversity, equity, and inclusion

  • Demonstrated commitment to valuing diversity and contributing to an inclusive working and learning environment

  • Master’s degree with major coursework in the field of assignment, plus at least three years of related experience; Additional related experience may substitute for required education

Preferreed Skills:

  • Experience providing supervision and guidance to other staff

  • Skills in Stata

  • Graduate-level coursework or applied experience in research methods, survey methodology, program evaluation, causal inference, or applied statistics

  • Experience with survey data tools (e.g., REDCap, Qualtrics)

  • Knowledge of and familiarity with topics related to early childhood and/or social policy

Coding Test Requirement:

As part of the selection process, competitive candidates will be asked to complete a 2-hour coding test. This test will assess your proficiency in coding, analyzing, and interpreting data. To complete the exercise, candidates will need access to a computer with R software.

At Vanderbilt University, we are intentional about and assume accountability for fostering advancement and respect for equity, diversity, and inclusion for all students, faculty, and staff. Our commitment to diversity makes us who we are. We have created a community that celebrates differences and lets individuality thrive. As part of this commitment, we actively value diversity in our workplace and learning environments as we seek to take advantage of the rich


backgrounds and abilities of everyone. The diverse voices of Vanderbilt represent an invaluable resource for the University in its efforts to fulfill its mission and strive to be an example of excellence in higher education.

title: Occupancy Planner, Corporate Real Estate – GREF, GREF Business Partnering
description:
The Global Real Estate and Facilities (GREF) team provides real estate transaction expertise, business partnering, occupancy planning, capital investment management, workplace strategy and facility operations for Amazon’s corporate office portfolio globally. This role is on the GREF Business Partnering (GBP) team who’s overarching purpose is to create a bridge between each business unit and GREF to align real estate strategies in support of business objectives. As a Manager on GREF’s Business Partnering team, you will serve as a Business Partner (BP) for AI and Security business units, working with the org's and GREF’s senior leaders.

Key job responsibilities
- Partner across enterprise partners (e.g., Finance, PXT, Public Relations, Legal, Security, etc.), all cross-functional GREF real estate teams, Corporate FP&A, and Public Policy to support executive leaders in managing through ambiguity while inspecting and understanding the consequences of choices and trade-offs.
- Build systems and tracking mechanisms to deliver agreed upon SLAs
- Establish rhythm of business for each org, integrating GREF into business-level OP1/OP2 planning process and WBR/MBR/QBR cadence
- Implement reporting mechanisms to support D&S leaders with data, analytics, metrics, and research to make informed decisions
- Balance business expectations and needs with Amazon fiduciary stewardship, as well as cost savings mandates and GREF standards/protocols
- Lead and support the development and delivery of S-team executive-level real estate presentations, recommendations, and business cases; incorporate input from GREF teams to secure decisions and alignment for those presentations
- Oversee issue escalation processes
- Partner with GREF teams and external stakeholders to drive the successful development, implementation, and execution of GREF and business strategies across organizations and regions
- Provide thought leadership, industry best practices and market insights to business leadership to inform recommendations and decisions

A day in the life
You'll develop plans and strategies that align with AI and Security headcount, specialty space (i.e., labs), and location requirements globally. These will be created and approved in partnership with AI/Security leadership, business finance and GREF cross-functional stakeholders.

About the team
Our core objective is to connect business operating plans to GREF's operating plan; to do so, we engage directly with stakeholders across all Amazon business orgs and GREF teams. As a result, we deliver business real estate requirements, real estate transaction rationale, and business line reporting.

description:
Position: Quality Assurance Associate (6 Month Contract)

Salary Range: $60,000 - $65,000/year

Location: Exton, PA (On-site)

About Pharmaron

Pharmaron is a global contract research and manufacturing organization (CRO/CDMO) helping pharma and biotech companies bring new therapies to life. With over 25,000 employees worldwide across 28 locations in the US, UK, China, and Singapore, we support drug discovery through to manufacturing with fully integrated high-quality services.

We're proud of the impact we make and just last year, we supported 887 discovery projects, 1,100+ CMC programs, and 1,397 clinical trials across all phases. Our teams are involved in everything from small molecules, ADC's, biologics, and gene therapies and we work with more than 3,300 global customers. To learn more, visit www.pharmaron.com.

What You'll Do

The Quality Assurance Generalist is responsible for ensuring the integrity and regulatory compliance of non-clinical laboratory studies by conducting systematic audits of study processes, data, and documentation in accordance with Good Laboratory Practice regulations for and providing support for GMP activities within the quality group.

Key Responsibilities

  • Audit each GLP study at intervals adequate to assure the integrity of the study and maintain documentation of each audit.
  • Submit to management and the study director written status reports on each study, noting any problems and the corrective actions taken.
  • Ensure that no deviations from approved protocols or standard operating procedures were made without proper authorization and documentation.
  • Review the final GLP study report to ensure that such report accurately describes the methods and standard operating procedures, and that the reported results accurately reflect the raw data of the GLP study.
  • Prepare and sign a statement to be included with the final GLP study report which shall specify the dates inspections were made and findings reported to management and the study director.
  • Maintain the Master Schedule.
  • Prepare internal audit reports and communicate findings to internal stakeholders.
  • Provide suitable recommendations for internal audit observations.
  • Track audit responses and drive closure of CAPAs resulting from internal audits.
  • Identify the potential compliance issues and champion continual process improvement.
  • Provide support during Regulatory inspections and client audits.
  • Perform client data review
  • Serve as resource for the Raw Material Program, receiving, quarantining and releasing materials for use by the laboratories
  • Involvement with controlled document systems, including authorizing, revising, and approving SOPs.
  • Provide support during regulatory inspections and client audits
  • This position may require occasional travel to visit other US Laboratory and CGT sites, attend conferences, training, or meeting with team members, stakeholders, vendors or suppliers. The GMP QA Manager should be prepared for up to 10% travel as needed.

What We're Looking For

  • Bachelor's degree in biology, chemistry, or related field.
  • 5 years of working within the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry.
  • Experience writing and reviewing SOPs, Protocols, Summary Reports
  • Experience with regulated data review
  • Excellent interpersonal skills with ability to communicate and work with all levels of the organization.
  • Excellent technical writing skills
  • Meticulous attention to detail

Why Pharmaron?

Pharmaron is a premier service provider for the life sciences industry. Founded in 2004, Pharmaron has invested in its people and facilities and established a broad spectrum of research, development, and manufacturing service capabilities throughout the entire drug discovery, preclinical, and clinical development process across multiple therapeutic modalities, including small molecules, biologics, and CGT products. With over 25,000 employees and operations in the US, UK, China, and Singapore. Pharmaron has an excellent track record in delivering R&D solutions to its partners in North America, Europe, Japan, and China.

Collaborative Culture: You will thrive in our inclusive and collaborative environment, where teamwork and innovation go hand in hand. Here, your voice matters, and your contributions make a real impact. "Employees Number One" and "Clients Centered" are the core cultural values at Pharmaron. Our culture, which sets Pharmaron apart from other organizations, has evolved from our deep commitment to our employees, partners, and collaborators.

How to Apply:

title: Senior Electrical Estimator - Airports & Infrastructure
description:
Senior Electrical Estimator

Company Overview
Would you enjoy being involved in executing large-scale, complex infrastructure projects?

Connico is a national construction consultancy known for its experienced team and commitment to exceptional client service. With deep experience in aviation and complex infrastructure, we are continuing to expand our work across energy, federal, and defense markets.

Our work is technical, but how we do the work matters just as much as the quality of what we deliver. Our core values of Respect, Integrity, Innovation, Resiliency, Inclusivity, and Thoughtfulness guide how we work with our clients and with one another.

The Role
As a Senior Electrical Estimator, you will lead complex electrical cost estimating efforts from early conceptual planning through final construction documents. You will use your technical experience and judgment to develop accurate estimates, identify scope gaps and risks, reconcile costs, and help clients make informed decisions, even when project information is limited or evolving.

This is a hands-on senior technical role. You will independently develop and review estimates while also helping strengthen Connico's electrical estimating practice through mentoring, quality control, knowledge sharing, and the development of repeatable estimating practices.

You will work across disciplines and directly with clients, project teams, contractors, designers, and other estimators on complex infrastructure projects.

What You'll Do

  • Lead and independently develop electrical cost estimates across all design stages, from conceptual and Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) estimates through final construction documents, including Level 1–5 estimates for projects of varying size and complexity.
  • Develop detailed material and labor estimates for electrical systems including Medium Voltage, Low Voltage, Communications, Audio-Visual, Security, Video Surveillance, and Fire Alarm systems. Research and develop unit pricing, cost assemblies, and supporting assumptions using current market information and sound estimating judgment.
  • Think beyond the plans and specifications. Identify missing information, scope gaps, inconsistencies, interdisciplinary conflicts, and potential cost risks. Develop well-supported assumptions and solutions when complete project information is not available.
  • Lead estimate reconciliations, technical and quality-control reviews, contractor bid analyses, value engineering assessments, life-cycle and benefit-cost analyses, and coordination across disciplines to produce comprehensive and defensible estimates.
  • Manage multiple complex estimating assignments and priorities while maintaining accuracy, meeting deadlines, and helping project teams deliver high-quality work that reflects Connico's standards and core values.
  • Mentor and train developing estimators in conceptual estimating, quantity takeoffs, cost buildups, reconciliations, technical reviews, interdisciplinary plan analysis, reporting, and Connico estimating practices. Help create training resources and repeatable best practices that strengthen the broader team.
  • Take ownership of estimating data, cost assemblies, templates, and reporting practices by helping maintain accurate, current, consistent, and accessible information that supports repeatable results.
  • Build strong client relationships and serve as a trusted technical advisor through clear communication, sound judgment, reliability, and expert guidance. Participate in client meetings, project site visits, and industry events as needed.
What You'll Bring
  • 10+ years of full-time, hands-on electrical estimating experience.
  • A Journeyman Electrician License, Master Electrician License, Electrical Engineering degree, or equivalent combination of electrical knowledge and experience.
  • An industry-recognized professional certification, license, or advanced credential, such as CCP, CPE, PCSE, CEP, CCE, PE, or another relevant advanced credential.
  • Proven ability to independently develop high-quality electrical estimates across Levels 1–5 and all stages of design, including conceptual and ROM estimates developed with limited information.
  • Demonstrated experience leading complex estimating assignments, integrating estimate elements across multiple disciplines, meeting deadlines, maintaining quality, and communicating professionally with clients and project stakeholders.
  • Strong ability to interpret architectural, civil, electrical, and other engineering drawings and specifications across all levels of design.
  • Expertise with electrical estimating or takeoff software such as IntelliBid, Accubid, On-Screen Takeoff, MII, MCACES, or comparable systems.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, Teams, Outlook, and Word.
Preferred Experience
  • Electrical estimating experience supporting aviation or airport projects is highly preferred.
  • Experience with other large-scale or complex project environments, including federal government, Department of Defense or military facilities, energy and utilities, transportation and infrastructure, industrial, mission-critical, or similar technically complex work, is valuable.

Travel
Minimal travel, up to 10%, may be required for client meetings, project or site visits, conferences and industry events, and visits to Connico office locations.

Why Join Connico?
This is an opportunity to do more than produce estimates. You will help solve complex cost challenges, influence the quality of major infrastructure projects, strengthen estimating practices, and develop the next generation of Connico estimators.

As Connico continues to grow beyond its established aviation and infrastructure work into energy, federal, and defense markets, you will also have the opportunity to apply your expertise across an expanding range of complex projects.

We value people who take ownership, bring solutions, share their expertise, challenge thinking thoughtfully, and build trust with clients and teammates. At the Senior level, you will be expected not only to demonstrate technical excellence, but also to help strengthen the people and practice around you.

If you are an experienced electrical estimator who combines strong technical expertise with sound judgment, leadership, and a commitment to quality, we would like to hear from you!

title: Senior Software Engineer - Webex
description:
Meet the Team

Cisco's Webex Engineering Group is redefining the future of collaboration. We're building a world where people connect effortlessly to enjoy modern, uncompromised collaboration across every room, desk, pocket, and application.

Focusing on AI features for the Webex Calling solution, our team works to integrate the latest artificial intelligence technologies to enable the next generation of collaboration, efficiency and innovation.

Our team is based in Galway. We operate a hybrid working model.
